title: UserHasSubscription ignores STRIPE_ENABLED=false (pro features locked server-side)
description:
Commit 0eb045e2 'Add STRIPE_ENABLED off-switch' wired StripeConfig into the Handler and made billing routes 404 + frontend unlock pro, but the backend gate was missed.

ProcessCardAfterCreation (handlers/cards.go:1336) calls Handler.UserHasSubscription (handlers/users.go:736), which returns services.UserHasSubscription (services/subscription.go) = stripe_subscription_status in (active, trialing). With STRIPE_ENABLED=false nobody ever gets an active status, so entity/fact extraction after card creation is silently skipped on every billing-less self-host, even though the frontend treats everyone as subscribed.

Fix: Handler.UserHasSubscription should return true when !s.StripeConfig.Enabled (mirror the frontend AuthContext logic). Add a test: STRIPE_ENABLED=false + user with 'free' status + card creation -> ProcessEntitiesAndFacts runs.
acceptance_criteria: With STRIPE_ENABLED=false, card creation processes entities/facts for users with no Stripe status; with billing enabled, behavior unchanged.
close_reason: Handler.UserHasSubscription returns true when StripeConfig.Enabled==false; services.UserHasSubscription unchanged as raw Stripe check. Tests: TestUserHasSubscriptionHonorsBillingSwitch. Landed 229e056d.

title: Bootstrap first admin on fresh self-host install
description:
On a brand-new instance, NO user can ever become admin, which makes the /admin UI and all admin-only routes unusable.

Evidence: users.is_admin defaults to false (schema.sqlite.sql:908); the only place that sets is_admin in production code is none (tests do it directly via SQL, tests/conftest.go:436); UpdateUserRoute (handlers/users.go:121) blocks non-admins from changing admin status; GitHub/OIDC flows never assign is_admin.

SaaS worked because the operator already had an admin account; a fresh self-host starts with zero admins and no promotion path.

Proposed fix (pick one or combine):
- First registered user becomes admin (guarded so it only happens once).
- Auto-promote the user whose email matches ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL (or a new ADMIN_EMAILS env var) on registration/OIDC provisioning.
- CLI/flag bootstrap (e.g. zg admin promote <email>) as a backstop.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh SQLite DB + first registered user yields an admin; existing installs unaffected; covered by a test.
close_reason: CreateUser now makes the first user on an empty install admin, plus ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL match (case-insensitive). Tests: TestCreateUserFirstUserBecomesAdmin, TestCreateUserAdminEmailGrantsAdmin. Landed 229e056d.

title: PUT /api/cards/<id> wipes card_id when omitted from partial update
description:
services/cards.go UpdateCard (line ~697) unconditionally executes UPDATE cards SET ..., card_id =  ... with params.CardID, and no 'preserve existing if nil' guard exists for card_id (unlike schema_id/structured_data, which are explicitly preserved when nil, lines 745-762). So a partial PUT without a card_id field (e.g. attaching schema_id + structured_data, as the pool-log workflow does: create shell via zg CLI then PUT structured_data) overwrites the card's card_id to empty string.

Secondary effect: DiscoverParentId('') + the parent lookup at lines 723-733 then set parent_id = cardPK (self-parent), silently corrupting the hierarchy for any card that had a parent.

Repro (observed live 2026-08-09, card 14676):
1. zg card create --card-id POOL2026.20 --title 2026-08-09 --body '...'
2. curl -X PUT /api/cards/14676 with {title, body, schema_id: 6, structured_data: {...}} (no card_id)
3. GET /api/cards/14676 -> card_id == "" (was POOL2026.20)
4. Fix for user: re-PUT including card_id. But API clients (zg CLI, MCP, sync engine) must not have to know this.

Fix: mirror the schema handling — if params.CardID is empty/unchanged, preserve oldCard.CardID (and skip the uniqueness + parent recompute, or recompute parent only when card_id actually changed). Add a regression test asserting partial updates without card_id keep the existing card_id and parent_id.

Related: Zettelgarden-pl3 (zg CLI epic; pool logging uses the CLI + raw API pattern), card_id preservation also matters for the sync push path.

title: Fix inverted --incomplete flags in zg task list/update
description: In task.go, --completed and --incomplete bind to the same bool var (taskListCompleted / taskUpdateIsComplete), so passing --incomplete sets the var to true: task list --incomplete sends completed=true (shows completed tasks) and task update --incomplete marks the task complete instead of incomplete. Fix: bind each flag to its own var (or derive the value from which flag changed, e.g. cmd.Flags().Changed('incomplete')).
close_reason: --completed/--incomplete and --complete/--incomplete bound to separate vars (14755c19)

title: Fix zg card list: GET /api/cards route no longer exists (use search endpoint)
description: zg card list (and --starred) calls GET /api/cards?limit=&offset=&starred= but the backend removed the general GET /api/cards route in Jan 2026 (fee32e9b). Only POST /api/cards is registered so GET returns 405. The web app lists cards via POST /api/search (empty query returns all cards). Fix: rewrite card list to call POST /api/search with the same filters (limit/offset/starred where supported) or re-add a GET /api/cards endpoint. Update README examples accordingly. Add a CLI test that exercises the search path.
close_reason: card list now uses POST /api/search; --starred uses GET /api/cards/starred (317a796d)

title: Fix zg task complete: runTaskComplete aliases runTaskUpdate which requires flags
description: zg task complete <id> delegates to runTaskUpdate, which builds a request body from flags and errors 'No updates' when none are set. So 'zg task complete 5' always fails. Fix: set is_complete=true (and status='done' like the MCP server does) when the complete subcommand is used. Keep 'zg task update <id> --complete' working.
close_reason: zg task complete now sends is_complete=true + status=done (a08518de)

title: Card connections: explain, discover, and visualize the note network
description:
Execute docs/plans/2026-08-09-card-connections-plan.md (reviewed by project reviewer agent 2026-08-09; audit of current state verified accurate). Goal: make relatedness trustworthy and actionable, give users active tools to grow connections, and make the network visible.

Current state: GET /api/cards/{id}/related exists (shared entities +3, shared tags +1, Typesense similarity scaled 0-10, hardcoded weights, top 10); reasons are computed but never rendered; related cards fetched once and cached (no refresh on save); no graph view, unlinked mentions, orphan report, or second-degree suggestions; no connection tooling in editor/MCP/CLI.

Phased (child issues): Phase 1 explainability + scoring control (reasons chips, RELATED_* env vars, refresh on save, group by reason). Phase 2 active discovery (unlinked mentions + add-link, orphan report, editor link suggestions, second-degree suggestions). Phase 3 visualization (interactive graph page, ego-network in rail, path finding). Phase 4 network intelligence + outward surfaces (entity hubs, network stats, MCP tools, zg CLI).

Known implementation constraints from review: backlinks table has no user_id column/PK (JOIN cards for ownership); GetCardsBySharedEntities/Tags return scores only (new SQL for names); orphan score must avoid per-card Typesense calls; editor suggestions gated to existing cards (no ID for /app/card/new); every new endpoint via addProtectedRoute.

title: FileVault: Typesense search results crash list for linked files (file.card undefined)
description:
## Context
When Typesense is configured, GetAllFilesRoute delegates to searchFilesInTypesense (handlers/files_typesense.go). The returned FileSearchResult struct omits the card object entirely (only file_id/name/type/size/card_pk/... are set; card is never populated).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run with Typesense enabled
2. In FileVault, search for a term that matches a file linked to a card (card_pk > 0)
3. FileListItem.tsx:269-271 renders `<Link to={`/app/card/${file.card.id}`}>` with no guard -> 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading id)' -> page crash

Note: FilesTab (card page) is unaffected because card-fetched files include card. The FileVault smoke test mocks the non-Typesense path so it never catches this.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Typesense search results include the linked card (populate Card via QueryPartialCardByID like the SQL path, or FileListItem guards file.card)
- No crash when searching linked files with Typesense enabled
- Test covers FileListItem rendering a Typesense-shaped result (missing card) without throwing
close_reason: Fixed and verified: EditFileMetadataRoute now persists/clears description (dynamic SQL + tests), all list/search paths return description, Typesense results populate card, FileListItem guards missing card (test added)

title: FileVault: file descriptions never persist (backend drops description on edit)
description:
## Context
FileMetadataEditor.tsx debounce-saves description via editFile() -> PATCH /files/:id with {name, card_pk, description}. The editor shows 'Saving...' and a success path, but the backend never writes the column.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open FileVault, open Edit Details on a file
2. Type a description, wait for the debounced autosave (500ms)
3. Reopen Edit Details (or search via Typesense) — description is empty
4. Inspect DB: files.description stays NULL

Root cause: go-backend/handlers/files.go EditFileMetadataRoute (~line 507) runs only `UPDATE files SET name = $1, card_pk = $2 WHERE id = $3` — description is ignored. Schema column exists (schema.sqlite.sql files.description), Typesense indexes it, but no write path exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- EditFileMetadataRoute persists description (and does not null it when omitted, unless explicitly cleared)
- Add/extend a Go test (handlers/files_test.go) covering description save + description clear
- Manual verify in FileVault: description survives reload and reopen of the editor
close_reason: Fixed and verified: EditFileMetadataRoute now persists/clears description (dynamic SQL + tests), all list/search paths return description, Typesense results populate card, FileListItem guards missing card (test added)

title: FileVault: fix broken upload/list paths + close KMS feature gaps
description:
## Context
Review of the FileVault feature (zettelkasten-front/src/pages/FileVault.tsx + components/files/* + go-backend handlers/files.go, files_typesense.go) found 7 bugs where UI behavior does not match intent (one silent data-loss feature, one page crash) plus 7 missing features that matter for a knowledge-management vault.

## Problem
- Description editing appears to save but the backend update statement never writes the column (silent data loss)
- Searching with Typesense enabled can crash the list for linked files and drops the storage quota + ignores filters/sort
- The documented filetype: search syntax always returns zero results
- Keyboard navigation (Enter/Delete) is broken/misleading with a stale-closure delete
- Double fetches on mount and per search; uploads clear active filters

## Success Criteria

- Feature issues in this epic are either closed or explicitly deferred with a note
- No regressions in existing FileVault smoke test; new tests cover fixed paths (Typesense search results, description persistence, filetype: filter)
- git push lands all changes (per repo landing-the-plane protocol)

## Non-Goals

- Multi-user shared vaults
close_reason: Epic complete: all 7 bugs fixed with tests (72f.1-72f.7); features 72f.8 + 72f.10 shipped; 72f.9/11/12/13/14 explicitly deferred with notes (allowed by epic success criteria); follow-up Zettelgarden-pvr tracks Typesense files-index wiring

title: Phase B: migrate all confirm flows to shared ui/ConfirmDialog (unify 4 implementations)
description:
Why: 4 incompatible confirm dialogs (tasks/admin/rss/tabs) with different prop names, looks, and a11y. Unifying them is the highest-leverage consistency win after the primitives exist.

Do:
- Migrate tasks/ConfirmDialog.tsx (3 live consumers) call sites to ui/ConfirmDialog
- Migrate admin/ConfirmDialog call sites (if any remain after the useConfirmDialog fix in z11.5) — note admin/ConfirmDialog itself is dead code (0 importers) and gets DELETED in Phase C, so migration here is about the hook consumers
- Migrate rss/RssConfirmDialog.tsx call sites
- Convert tabs/RollbackConfirmDialog.tsx to a thin specialization on ui/ConfirmDialog (custom change-preview body, shared shell)
- Run test:run + format:check + build + e2e/smoke.ts after

Acceptance Criteria:
- All confirm flows route through ui/ConfirmDialog; only RollbackConfirmDialog remains as a thin specialization
- One API in use; no call site passes variant/severity/dangerous/onCancel ad-hoc props
- test:run, format:check, build, e2e/smoke.ts green
close_reason: All confirm flows now route through ui/ConfirmDialog. Migrated: tasks TaskListItem/TaskSubtasksSection/TaskDialog (3 consumers, import + drop redundant variant='danger' — danger is the default), RssPage (RssConfirmDialog -> ui/ConfirmDialog, dangerous={true} dropped), RollbackConfirmDialog converted to a thin specialization on ui/ConfirmDialog (custom change-preview body via new children slot; early-return guard for null auditEvent restored; Restoring... button keeps ui/Spinner via ReactNode confirmText). admin/ConfirmDialog had 0 importers (dead code, deleted Phase C) so no hook consumers to migrate. ConfirmDialog API grew optional children slot + ReactNode confirmText/cancelText; message now optional. Gates: test:run 881 pass, format:check clean, build OK, DESKTOP E2E SMOKE PASSED (fresh + session scenarios).

title: Phase A: ui/ConfirmDialog + fix useConfirmDialog cancel-path bug (one API for 4 implementations)
description:
Why: 4 incompatible confirm dialogs exist — tasks/ConfirmDialog.tsx (raw, variant prop, default danger, 3 live consumers), admin/ConfirmDialog.tsx (raw, severity prop, escape+scroll-lock+checkbox, useConfirmDialog hook is DEAD CODE with 0 importers AND has a real bug: only calls resolve() in onConfirm, so cancelling leaves await confirm(...) hanging forever), rss/RssConfirmDialog.tsx (Headless, dangerous:boolean, animation), tabs/RollbackConfirmDialog.tsx (raw custom change-preview body). Different prop names (variant vs severity vs dangerous, onClose vs onCancel), different look, different a11y. A consumer cannot predict the API or look.

Do:
- Baseline decision required (recorded in notes): either fix admin's useConfirmDialog cancel path (resolve(false) on cancel + tests) or derive the API from tasks/ConfirmDialog (3 live consumers) and fold in admin's Escape/scroll-lock/checkbox. Recommend: build ui/ConfirmDialog on top of ui/Modal (z11.1), API derived from tasks/ConfirmDialog + admin's a11y features, and keep useConfirmDialog with the cancel bug FIXED.
- Create src/components/ui/ConfirmDialog.tsx on Modal: title/message/cancel/confirm, severity or variant prop, Escape + scroll-lock inherited from Modal, optional checkbox
- Fix the useConfirmDialog cancel-path bug (resolve false on cancel) and add tests
- Keep tabs/RollbackConfirmDialog as a thin specialization on top of the shared ConfirmDialog/Modal (its custom change-preview body stays, but shell/API comes from the primitive)
- Vitest spec: confirm resolves true, cancel resolves false (no hang), Escape closes

Acceptance Criteria:
- ui/ConfirmDialog exists on ui/Modal, one API surface
- useConfirmDialog cancel path resolves (no hanging await); test proves it
- tasks/ConfirmDialog, admin/ConfirmDialog, rss/RssConfirmDialog, tabs/RollbackConfirmDialog all either migrate here or are recorded as superseded for Phase C deletion
- Vitest specs green
close_reason: BASELINE DECISION (recorded per issue): API derived from tasks/ConfirmDialog (3 live consumers) — isOpen/onClose/onConfirm/title/message/confirmText/cancelText/variant(derived 'danger' default) — with admin/ConfirmDialog's a11y + safety features folded in (Escape + scroll-lock via ui/Modal, optional requireCheckbox/checkboxLabel, details text). severity/dangerous/onCancel variants are gone. useConfirmDialog KEPT with the cancel-path bug FIXED (resolve(false) on cancel/Escape via resolveRef; pending promise resolved false before a new confirm opens) and moved into ui/ConfirmDialog.tsx. Superseded status recorded: tasks/ConfirmDialog, admin/ConfirmDialog, rss/RssConfirmDialog = Phase C deletion; tabs/RollbackConfirmDialog stays as thin specialization on ConfirmDialog/Modal (custom body only) — call-site migration is z11.9. Vitest specs: ConfirmDialog (5) + useConfirmDialog resolves true/false/Escape-no-hang (3). Gates: test:run 849 pass, format:check clean, tsc clean, build OK.

title: Subagent review: notifications contract bug fixed (unread_count + total)
description:
Why: subagent code review of a5q.4/a5q.6 found a real prod bug. The notification contract was mismatched between Go backend and the React client, silently breaking the inbox indicators:
- GET /api/notifications/unread-count returned {"count": n} but the frontend read response.unread_count -> "X unread" indicator and the document title badge (Notifications (N)) rendered nothing.
- GET /api/notifications returned {"notifications": [...]} with NO total, but the page read response.total -> "X total" indicator hidden.
The page rendered the list fine, so the bug was invisible in normal use.

FIXED in commit 7702a0f0 (this issue can be closed):
- handlers/notifications.go: GetUnreadCount now returns {"unread_count": count}; ListNotifications now includes "total" (via new models.CountNotificationsByUser, same filters, no limit/offset).
- notifications_test.go: TestGetUnreadCountSuccess asserts unread_count; TestListNotificationsSuccess asserts total >= 3.
- NotificationInboxPage.smoke.test.tsx now asserts "2 unread" renders, so a future contract drift fails the test (the exact regression the a5q epic exists to catch: my original smoke test mirrored the wrong frontend types and passed while the page was broken).

Also from the same review (see Zettelgarden-8q3 for the infra side):
- setup.ts adds an explicit /rss/unread-counts default (RSSProvider mounts in every renderWithProviders test; previously the fetch failed loudly and was only silenced by the provider .catch).
- SearchPage smoke test stubs /schemas locally (SearchFiltersPanel fetches on mount).

Acceptance: unread/total indicators render in prod; smoke test fails if the key ever drifts again; backend + frontend suites green.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 7702a0f0: GetUnreadCount returns unread_count (was count), ListNotifications now includes total via new models.CountNotificationsByUser; backend tests updated to assert both keys; NotificationInboxPage smoke test now asserts '2 unread' renders so future drift fails the suite. Backend + frontend suites green.

title: Frontend test suite exits 1: 4 unhandled rejections in Sidebar.test.tsx (a5q.5 regression)
description:
Why: the a5q.5 landmine removal (remove catch-all fetch mock, fail loudly) left the frontend suite RED at the gate: `npm run test:run` and `npm run test:coverage` report 656/656 tests passing but exit code 1. Verified with CI=true too, so the frontend CI "Run Tests" step fails. This directly undercuts the a5q epic goal (a green suite that doesn't lie) and will infect a5q.6 page smoke tests, which mount the full provider stack. The a5q.5 close note "verified no test silently depended on the {} catch-all" is inaccurate: Sidebar.test.tsx silently depended on it for /rss/folders and the TagProvider /tags fetch.

Root cause (two compounding bugs):
1. src/tests/setup.ts registers provider-stack defaults (/task-statuses, /tags, /tasks?) in beforeAll, but afterEach calls resetMockEndpoints(), which wipes the defaults after the FIRST test of each file. Sidebar output proves it: test 1 fails only on /rss/folders; tests 2-5 additionally fail on /task-statuses because the default is gone. Same trap will hit any per-file beforeAll registrations (a5q.6).
2. Sidebar.test.tsx mounts TagProvider WITHOUT testing=true, so it does a real /tags fetch; TagContext.getTags() is the only provider fetch without a .catch (StatusContext/RSSContext both catch). The loud failure becomes an unhandled rejection, setup.ts process.on(unhandledRejection) rethrows it, and vitest records 4 Unhandled Errors -> exit 1.

Do:
- Register defaults in beforeEach (or make resetMockEndpoints preserve them)
- Pass testing=true testTags=[] to TagProvider in Sidebar.test.tsx (consistent with renderWithProviders)
- Add a .catch to TagContext.getTags() (latent prod gap too: a failed tags fetch is an unhandled rejection in the browser)

Acceptance: `npm run test:run` and `npm run test:coverage` exit 0 with zero Unhandled Errors; CI Run Tests step green.
close_reason: Fixed: (1) src/tests/setup.ts registers provider-stack defaults in beforeEach instead of beforeAll so resetMockEndpoints() in afterEach no longer wipes them after the first test of each file; (2) Sidebar.test.tsx passes testing=true testTags=[] to TagProvider and stubs /rss/folders explicitly (Sidebar fetches it on mount); (3) TagContext.getTags() now catches fetch failures (was the only provider fetch without a .catch — also a latent prod unhandled-rejection gap). Result: npm run test:run and npm run test:coverage exit 0 (were 1), zero Unhandled Errors, 656/656 tests green, typecheck + format:check clean. Bonus: act() warnings 78 -> 61 (Sidebar fetches now settle instead of failing mid-test).

title: Sync push: retried update/delete (dropped response) is mislabeled conflict + counts a lost edit
description:
Found in code review of v5b (tsv/nqx). The push apply loop's idempotency shortcut only covers creates (BaseVersion == 0). When the server applies an update or delete but the response is lost (flaky network), the client retries the SAME outbox entry with its original base_version; the server has advanced the row version, so the retry hits 'stale base' and returns status=conflict with lost_edits incremented.

Verified with probe tests against current tree: update retry -> status=conflict serverVersion=2 lostEdits=1; delete retry -> same. Data converges (client adopts its own row) but the UI will surface spurious lost-edit counts on ordinary network failures, violating the nqx 'retries idempotent' and tsv 'idempotent retry produces no duplicates' acceptance criteria.

Fix direction: on a stale base_version, compare the pushed payload against the current server row; if identical (or version == base+1 with matching data), return applied with no lost edit instead of conflict.,
acceptance_criteria: Re-push of the same update/delete entry (base_version unchanged) after a successful-but-lost response returns status=applied and adds 0 lost edits; a genuinely stale concurrent edit still returns conflict + lost edit. Handler tests for update-retry and delete-retry cover both cases. Go tests green.
close_reason: Fixed: retryOrConflict/retryMatchesCurrent in sync_apply.go treat a stale base as an idempotent retry when version == base+1 AND the re-pushed payload matches the current row (upserts) or the row is already soft-deleted (deletes) — reported applied with 0 lost edits. Genuinely stale concurrent edits (different content, or >1 version jump) still conflict + count a lost edit. Per-collection matchers handle card_id normalization, structured_data semantic compare, task uuid-FK resolution and time fields, NULL-safe scans. New handler tests: update-retry, delete-retry, task update-retry, stale-update-vs-delete discriminator. Full go test ./... green; landed 84375393.

title: Local-first sync: mobile + desktop apps
description:
Execute docs/plans/2026-08-07-mobile-desktop-sync-app-design.md (3 review passes, signed off 2026-08-08). Goal: native desktop (Tauri v2) + mobile (React Native WebView shell) clients with real offline-first sync — local SQLite mirror + outbox, server as sync hub (snapshot/changes/push), optimistic-concurrency last-write-wins, server-derived junctions pull-only, tags name-keyed merge. Web SPA stays a thin client.

Resolved decisions (from design recommendations): rung 2 (offline read + write, LWW); Tauri desktop; RN shell + WebView mobile; TypeScript sync engine; offline-writable scope = cards, tasks, tags only (card_tags/task_tags are server-derived and pull-only; offline tagging = body/title text edit).

Phased: 0 backend sync API (critical path), 1 shared TS sync engine, 2 Tauri desktop, 3 RN mobile, 4 polish. Phase 0 pinned tables: cards, tasks, tags (junctions derived).

title: Convert python-mail service to Go (embed SMTP in backend)
description:
Goal: eliminate the separate Flask mailer (python-mail/) so self-hosting is one Go binary + SQLite (fewer services to run, one language, no ZETTEL_MAIL_* env duplication).

Current architecture:
- go-backend/mail.MailClient (mail/mail.go) POSTs JSON to m.Host + '/api/send' with Authorization: m.Password — the python service does the actual SMTP.
- python-mail/app.py exposes /api/send, /api/send/mailing-list, /health; hard-crashes at boot without ZETTEL_MAIL_SERVER/USERNAME/PASSWORD/DEFAULT_SENDER.
- docker-compose.yml always deploys mail-service (python image) on :8081; MAIL_HOST=localhost / MAIL_PASSWORD are the Go side's pointer into it.

Plan:
- Replace the HTTP hop with direct SMTP in Go (net/smtp or a maintained lib; keep the existing MailClient API/queue so callers don't change).
- Keep or fold the mailing-list email path (see mailing-list removal bead — if that lands first, /api/send/mailing-list dies with it).
- Remove python-mail/, its Dockerfile, the compose mail-service, and the ZETTEL_MAIL_* / MAIL_HOST / MAIL_PASSWORD wiring.
- Coordinate with 6er.6 (mail optional): MAIL_ENABLED=false + auto-validate email becomes the no-mail self-host path.

Acceptance: docker compose up runs without the mail-service container; transactional email (validation, password reset, reminders) is sent by the Go backend directly; python-mail/ deleted.
acceptance_criteria: docker compose up runs without the mail-service container; transactional email is sent by the Go backend directly; python-mail/ deleted.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (2026-08-07 audit of python-mail):

WHAT THE PYTHON SERVICE DOES (python-mail/app.py):
1. POST /api/send — one transactional email: subject/recipient/body/is_html; sender ('Zettelgarden', DEFAULT_SENDER); 400 if no subject/recipient, 500 on SMTP failure.
2. POST /api/send/mailing-list — TO + BCC lists. DEAD CODE from the Go backend's perspective: SendMailingListMessage (mail/mailing_list.go) loops per-recipient via SendHTMLEmail and never hits this endpoint. Dies with 6er.11.
3. GET /health — no-op in-process.
SMTP: ZETTEL_MAIL_SERVER, port 587 default, MAIL_USE_TLS=True (STARTTLS), username/password auth, DEFAULT_SENDER. File logging (ZETTEL_MAIL_LOG).

GO PORT SCOPE:
1. SMTP transport — net/smtp is insufficient (built-in auth only PLAIN/CRAM-MD5, no implicit TLS, no MIME, no RFC 2047, no timeouts). Use a maintained lib (github.com/go-mail/mail or wneessen/go-mail) to mirror Flask-Mail: STARTTLS 587 + implicit TLS 465, PLAIN/LOGIN auth, dial/send timeouts so a dead SMTP server can't wedge the queue.
2. MIME construction: From ('Zettelgarden <from@...>'), To, Subject RFC 2047-encoded (welcome subject has emoji: 'Welcome to Zettelgarden! 🌱'), Date, MIME-Version, text/plain vs text/html (gomarkdown HTML bodies), UTF-8 Content-Transfer-Encoding.
3. Config consolidation: merge MAIL_HOST/MAIL_PASSWORD (Go) + ZETTEL_MAIL_SERVER/USERNAME/PASSWORD/DEFAULT_SENDER (python) into one set: host:port, username, password, from, TLS mode. Fold in 6er.6 semantics (unset = disabled, no crash, no banner nag via auto-validate).
4. Update all MailClient constructions: main.go:163, cmd/reminders/main.go:19, tests/conftest.go:224. Keep queue/retry(4x,1s)/shutdown-drain/Testing-bypass in mail/mail.go unchanged — only sendMailImpl swaps HTTP POST -> SMTP.
5. Deployment cleanup: delete python-mail/, drop mail-service from both compose files (stops build.sh building it), replace ZETTEL_MAIL_* docs in .env.example with consolidated block.

SEQUENCING: do WITH 6er.11 (mailing-list removal deletes SendMailingListMessage/SendWelcomeEmail/HandleAddToMailingList -> only single-recipient path remains) and AFTER/ALONGSIDE 6er.6 (mail optional). Suggested order: 6er.11 first, then 6er.12+6er.6 as one change touching the mail surface once.
IMPLEMENTED in branch zg-6er12 (commit 4b410a30, pushed to origin, not yet merged to master — merge blocked by concurrent agents on the shared tree; only README.md expected conflict).

Summary: wneessen/go-mail v0.8.1; MailClient sendMailImpl delivers directly over SMTP (STARTTLS default, implicit TLS 465, plain when SMTP_STARTTLS=false; 10s dial/30s send timeouts; PLAIN auth when creds present; RFC 2047 + HTML handled by lib). Config MAIL_HOST/MAIL_PASSWORD -> SMTP_HOST/SMTP_PORT/SMTP_USERNAME/SMTP_PASSWORD/SMTP_FROM/SMTP_STARTTLS; MAIL_ENABLED auto-detect preserved; prod validation requires SMTP_HOST+SMTP_FROM when enabled. Verified: go test ./... green, tsc green. TO MERGE: git merge origin/zg-6er12 (needs quiet tree), then close.

Direct SMTP in Go (wneessen/go-mail v0.8.1): STARTTLS default, implicit TLS 465, plain when SMTP_STARTTLS=false; 10s/30s timeouts; PLAIN auth when creds set; RFC 2047 + HTML via lib. title: Make mail optional (MAIL_ENABLED=false) for self-hosters without SMTP
description:
Mail is effectively mandatory today:
- Go config requires MAIL_HOST + MAIL_PASSWORD (pkg/config/services.go:122-123).
- python-mail hard-crashes at startup without ZETTEL_MAIL_SERVER/USERNAME/PASSWORD/DEFAULT_SENDER (python-mail/app.py check_required_env_vars).
- docker-compose.yml always deploys mail-service.
- Registration tells users 'Check your email for a validation email'; the EmailValidationBanner nags forever when no mail is configured.

Fix:
- MAIL_ENABLED=false (or auto-detect empty MAIL_HOST): skip MailClient init, tolerate send failures everywhere (already mostly logged), don't require the vars.
- EMAIL_AUTO_VALIDATE=true for billing-less/self-host: treat new accounts as email_validated so the banner never appears (or hide the banner when mail is off).
- python-mail: make env vars optional at boot (fail per-request instead of crash) or allow the service to be omitted from compose.
- Task reminders / notifications should degrade gracefully (already log-and-continue).
acceptance_criteria: An instance with MAIL_ENABLED=false (no SMTP) boots, registers users, and shows no email-validation banner.

title: Convert Zettelgarden from SaaS target to purely self-hosted app
description:
Audit findings (2026-08-07) for converting Zettelgarden from a SaaS-targeted product to a purely self-hosted app, with billing (Stripe) as an optional add-on.

Already done: SQLite-only (Postgres retired), local file storage (S3/B2 retired), STRIPE_ENABLED off-switch (routes 404, UI hides paywalls, pro unlocked in frontend), opt-in OIDC, disableable GitHub OAuth, graceful Typesense fallback.

title: Phase 6a: replace Postgres '~' regex in GetNextRootCardID (cards.go) — missed Phase 3 PG-ism
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). Phase 3's PG-ism inventory checked ARRAY[ and = ANY($1) but NOT the Postgres regex match operator '~'. Two call sites survive:

- services/cards.go:810 — GetNextRootCardID: AND card_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'
- handlers/cards.go:494 — (s *Handler) getNextRootCardID: AND card_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'

SQLite has no '~' regex operator (REGEXP requires a user-defined function). The query errors silently, returns empty, and GetNextRootCardID falls back to '1' instead of the correct MAX(numeric)+1. This breaks 3 handler tests (TestGetNextRootCardID, TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute, contributes to TestGetNextChildCardID) and is a REAL production bug post-cutover: every new root card would collide on id '1'.

Note these are duplicate implementations (services + handlers both inline the SQL). The handlers copy is the legacy dup; services.GetNextRootCardID is the canonical one (called from handlers/epub.go).

Fix: no cross-driver SQL expresses 'pure digits' (LIKE has no char classes on either DB; GLOB is SQLite-only). Pull the filter into Go: SELECT candidate card_id WHERE user_id/is_deleted, then filter with regexp.MustCompile('^[0-9]+$').MatchString and take the max via strconv.Atoi. At single-user scale this is trivial. Ideally dedupe the two impls onto the services one and have the handler call it.

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a. Blocks the cards-id cluster of Zettelgarden-j89.
acceptance_criteria: GetNextRootCardID works identically on Postgres and SQLite; the '~' operator is gone from services/cards.go and handlers/cards.go; TestGetNextRootCardID, TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute green on SQLite; no other PG regex operators remain in non-test Go (grep clean).
close_reason: Fixed in de7b122e. services.GetNextRootCardID now filters pure-numeric ids in Go (regexp) — no '~' operator remains in non-test Go (grep clean). Deduped the handler copy onto it. TestGetNextRootCardID + TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute green on SQLite; full services/server/models/routes packages still green; handlers failures 11 -> 9.

title: ViewPageHeader/EditPageHeader nav & icon buttons show teal bg (missing variant on ui/Button migration)
description:
Regression from Zettelgarden-z11.10 (commit 2b0847bc 'Migrate header button surfaces to ui/Button'). Buttons migrated to ui/Button without a variant prop default to variant='primary' (bg-palette-dark #38a3a5), so ‹ Prev / ↑ Up / Next ›, Star, info-pane toggle, ＋ Child (ViewPageHeader) and suggest-title, info-pane toggle (EditPageHeader) now render with a teal/green background where they used to be transparent. Also hover:bg-palette-darkest (primary) beats consumer hover overrides (extended palette classes sort last in Tailwind), so hover feedback is wrong too.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open any card in the app (ViewPage).
2. Look at the ‹ Prev / ↑ Up / Next › cluster under the title (or the Star / info-pane icon buttons, or ＋ Child).
3. Observe the teal/green background (bg-palette-dark #38a3a5) where pre-migration (before commit 2b0847bc) the buttons were transparent with gray text.
4. Same on the Edit page (EditPageHeader): suggest-title icon and info-pane toggle show the teal bg.

## Fix
Add a 'ghost' variant to ui/Button (bg-transparent hover:bg-gray-100 focus:ring-gray-500, no text color so consumers keep exact control) and use it on the affected buttons. Bonus: fix dead class typo hover:bg-palette-lighest -> palette-lightest in EditPageHeader suggest-title.
acceptance_criteria: All header buttons that were transparent pre-migration render transparent again (no bg-palette-dark); ui/Button gains ghost variant with Vitest coverage; npm run test:run, format:check, tsc, build pass.
close_reason: Fixed: added ui/Button 'ghost' variant (bg-transparent, no text color) and applied it to the 8 migrated header buttons (Star, info-pane, Prev/Up/Next, ＋Child in ViewPageHeader; suggest-title, info-pane in EditPageHeader) that had defaulted to primary's bg-palette-dark teal background. Vitest ghost spec added; targeted suites + tsc + build green. NOTE: ViewPageContainer.test.tsx (3) and ViewPage.smoke.test.tsx (2) fail both before and after this change — pre-existing from unrelated in-progress references/related-cards work, tracked separately.

title: c6l.3 Keychain auth + token injection/revocation (mobile)
description:
Mobile credential story (design: Phase 3 — token in native keychain, NOT localStorage inside the webview; injected per navigation, revoked on logout).

- react-native-keychain stores the JWT in the OS keychain.
- Webview shim (injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded): window.zgMobile API + localStorage interception for token/username keys → keychain via the bridge — mirrors desktop preload.js createShim (async prime, per-key serialized writes, clear() covers keychain keys, legacy localStorage migration).
- Token injected per navigation: RN pushes the current token in on every navigation (onNavigationStateChange / before load); logout revokes → keychain delete + shim returns null → AuthContext boots to login. The webview never persists the token itself.
- AuthContext: generalize the desktop keychain-priming branch (zgDesktop.ready) to the mobile bridge (zgMobile.ready); offline restart keeps session with cached profile (desktop pattern).
acceptance_criteria: Login persists across app restart (keychain); logout clears keychain + webview session; offline restart keeps session with cached profile; no code path writes the token to webview localStorage.
close_reason: c6l.3 complete. The JWT lives in the OS keychain (react-native-keychain), never in WebView localStorage. Mobile: src/keychain.ts stores the (username, JWT) pair per service with merging key-level writes; src/bridge.ts dispatches keychain_get/set/delete; webviewShim.js createShim gained the keychain-backed localStorage proxy ported from desktop preload.js — async prime reads the keychain, per-key serialized write queues (logout-then-login cannot reorder), clear() covers the keychain keys, legacy plaintext tokens in webview storage migrate into the keychain and are removed from the webview, and token/username reads hit the keychain (never webview storage). Token injection per navigation: every page load re-primes from the keychain (injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded); the SPA never persists the token itself. Logout revocation: AuthContext.logoutUser does localStorage.removeItem('token') → shim queues keychain_delete → JWT gone → next boot goes to login. Offline restart keeps the session: shim.ready primes the keychain before AuthContext reads the token (c6l.4's waitForShellReady covers the mobile bridge); cached-profile restore already handled by AuthContext's isNativeShell branch. Fixed a var closure-capture bug in the migration loop (now const per-iteration bindings). Tests: 17 new mobile tests (keychain store round-trip/merge, bridge keychain commands, shim localStorage interception incl. legacy migration, per-key ordering, clear/getToken) — 39 total, tsc/lint/prettier clean, assembleDebug green (react-native-keychain autolinked). Acceptance: login persists across restart (keychain); logout clears keychain + webview session; offline restart keeps session with cached profile; no code path writes the token to webview localStorage — all met at the unit/bridge level; on-device run-verify remains c6l.5 (KVM constraint noted there). Landed 28eff7b2.

title: c6l.1 RN shell scaffold (mobile/)
description:
RN shell (design: Phase 3, c6l scope). New mobile/ package: React Native 0.7x (new architecture) + react-native-webview + op-sqlite + react-native-keychain hosting the existing zettelkasten-front Vite build.

- Dev mode: WebView loads the Vite dev server (or Metro). Prod: embed dist built with base './' (new vite.config.mobile.ts), served via file:// WebView source with no dev-server dependency.

title: c6l.5 Simulator verification + desktop↔mobile convergence smoke
description:
Verification for the Phase 3a acceptance criteria (design: Phase 3 exit criteria).

title: c6l.2 WebView↔RN postMessage bridge + MobileStorageAdapter
description:
The bridge (design: Phase 3 + review item 8 — op-sqlite runs on the RN JS thread, NOT inside the WebView; the mobile SQLiteAdapter IS the bridge).

- Request/response bridge with ids: webview calls window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage({id, cmd, args}); RN resolves via injectJavaScript. Commands mirror the desktop sync_db.rs surface: begin/exec/query/commit/rollback + ping, executed against op-sqlite on the RN JS thread.
- MobileStorageAdapter in the webview implements the async StorageAdapter contract (mirror of TauriStorageAdapter): transaction() serialization queue (BEGIN/COMMIT must not interleave across bridge round-trips), JSON data column, outbox coalescing keeping the first base_version, mirror schema identical (sync_meta, mirror_rows, sync_outbox) created by whenReady migrate.
- Tests: bridge protocol unit tests (mock postMessage/injectJavaScript); adapter passes the same matrix as TauriStorageAdapter; harness scenario running MobileStorageAdapter against the live backend (two-device convergence is engine-level and already covered by sync-engine/harness — add one mobile-adapter scenario).
acceptance_criteria: MobileStorageAdapter implements the full StorageAdapter contract and passes the engine adapter tests; bridge protocol unit tests green; a harness scenario with MobileStorageAdapter converges against the live Go backend.
close_reason: c6l.2 complete. Mobile: src/sqlite.ts wraps op-sqlite on the RN JS thread (BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/exec/query/reset, single connection — never inside the WebView); src/bridge.ts dispatches sql_begin/exec/query/commit/rollback + db_reset mirroring desktop sync_db.rs; webviewShim exposes generic zgMobile.invoke. Frontend: data/mobileStorageAdapter.ts implements the full async StorageAdapter contract over the bridge (tx serialization queue, outbox coalescing keeping first base_version, identical sync_meta/mirror_rows/sync_outbox schema, plain ? params — portable to op-sqlite and the Node loopback); syncClient.buildStorageAdapter selects it in the mobile shell, so mobile card/task/tag reads/writes now route through SyncDataProvider (engine mirror + outbox) — the c6l.4 acceptance item that was gated here is now wired. Tests: mobile 6 new bridge-command tests (22 total); engine 8 new mobile-adapter tests = the sqlite-adapter matrix ported over a loopback bridge to a real better-sqlite3 executor (48 total). Harness scenario 11: MobileStorageAdapter (bridge→SQLite) + desktop SqliteStorageAdapter share one account; offline edits on the phone reconcile; all mirrors converge — verified against the live Go backend (11/11). One observed SQLITE_BUSY flake in scenario 05 on a cold run (backend busy-retry path), green on re-run. Gates: FE 940, engine 48, mobile 22, tsc/lint/prettier clean, assembleDebug green (op-sqlite autolinked). Landed 80fcaf06.

title: zg CLI: durable auth — support long-lived API keys + secure token storage
description:
The zg CLI authenticates with a JWT pasted into ~/.config/zettelgarden/config.json (plain JSON, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'). Problem: backend JWTs expire after 15 days, so CLI auth silently breaks and the user must re-copy a token from the web UI. The backend already supports long-lived API Keys (RegisterAPIKeyRoutes, Settings -> API Keys in the app; models/api_key.go hashes keys at rest) which work with the same Bearer header.

Goal: make zg CLI auth durable so it doesn't rot every 15 days.

Proposed scope:
1. Document/switch the README and config.example.json to API keys instead of session JWTs (epic item 7 touches this — make it actionable here).
2. Add a 'zg auth' command group: 'zg auth login' (device-style or username/password exchange to mint an API key via the backend) and/or 'zg auth status' showing key name + expiry/rotation info. At minimum, a documented flow to create an API key from the web UI and store it.
3. Stop storing the token in a world-readable plaintext JSON (0600 perms at least; ideally integrate with the OS keyring, e.g. keyring/secret-service, with env var fallback per Zettelgarden-pl3.6).
4. Precedence: env (ZETTELGARDEN_TOKEN) > keyring > config file, keeping current flag overrides working.
5. Tests for auth resolution + a warning when the configured token is a known-short-lived JWT format.

Do not duplicate: Zettelgarden-pl3.6 (env var overrides only) and epic item 7 (README truthfulness). This issue is the mechanism itself.
close_reason: Closed

title: zg CLI: repair and align with current app
description:
# zg CLI: repair and align with current app

Full-stack audit of `zg/` (the standalone Go CLI) against the current backend routes (`go-backend/routes/`), the web app (`zettelkasten-front/`), and the MCP server (`zettelgarden-mcp/`). The CLI was last meaningfully updated May 2026 (fact removal); the backend/app have moved on (345+ commits since). Result: broken commands, stale README documenting removed features, dead code, flag bugs, and a large feature-parity gap vs. the app and the MCP server.

## Audit summary

### Broken against current backend
1. **`zg card list` (and `--starred`) is broken.** It calls `GET /api/cards?limit=&offset=&starred=` but the backend removed the general `GET /api/cards` route in Jan 2026 (commit fee32e9b "Remove GET /api/cards route (don't want general cards endpoint)"). Only `POST /api/cards` is registered, so GET returns 405. The app lists cards via `POST /api/search` (empty query = all cards); the CLI must switch to search or a new endpoint.
2. **`zg task complete <id>` is broken.** `runTaskComplete` just aliases `runTaskUpdate`, which requires at least one flag; with no flags it errors "No updates". The MCP server does this correctly (`is_complete=True`, `status="done"`).
3. **`zg task list --incomplete` / `zg task update --incomplete` are inverted.** Both `--completed` and `--incomplete` bind to the *same* bool var, so `--incomplete` sends `completed=true` → shows/marks tasks as complete instead of incomplete.

### Dead code
4. **`zg article create` exists but is never registered.** `internal/cmd/article.go` defines `GetArticleCmd()`, but `main.go` only registers card/task/template. Backend `POST /api/articles` works and the app supports article creation.

### Removed features still referenced
5. **README documents `zg fact ...` commands** (get/list/update/delete/similar/link/merge) but `fact.go` was deleted May 2026 (commit 29d29667 "Remove fact commands from zg CLI"). The binary has no fact commands. (Backend fact routes still exist; the frontend is mid-removal — FactPage remains but is hidden from the sidebar and plans refer to facts as removed in `qsg`. Decision needed: fully remove from README, or restore CLI commands while backend endpoints live.)

### Documentation gaps
6. README omits commands that exist: `card summaries`, `card next-id`, `card next-child-id`.
7. README says "Get your token from the Zettelgarden web UI" but JWT expires after 15 days; the app now has API Keys (Settings → API Keys) that are stable and work with the same Bearer header.
8. Design doc (`docs/plans/2026-03-01-zg-cli-design.md`) specifies `ZETTELGARDEN_TOKEN` / `ZETTELGARDEN_API_URL` env overrides; neither is implemented.

### Feature gaps vs app / MCP (non-exhaustive)
- Star/unstar cards; card children/tree/references/related/audit; tags CRUD; schemas list/get (CLI requires schema-id for structured data but can't discover schemas); parse_url; unsorted cards; suggest-title.
- Task advanced: subtasks, dependencies, reorder, complete-and-schedule, parent, statuses CRUD, saved searches.
- Files, entities, RSS, stats, notifications, summarize create/list, sync API, jobs, API-key management.

## Scope of this epic
Fix the broken/dangerous items (1–3), wire up or remove dead code (4), make docs truthful (5–7), implement design-doc env overrides (8), and add the highest-value missing commands (star/unstar, children, tags, schemas, parse_url). Full parity with every app surface is out of scope here; create follow-up tasks for the long tail.

Related: Zettelgarden-9ux.15 (zg CLI related/orphans/suggest commands) — do not duplicate.

title: Second-degree suggestions: refs of refs
description:
From plan Phase 2.4. Collaborative-style signal: cards referenced by cards that reference the source card, scored by overlap, excluding already-linked cards.

Backend: extend GET /api/cards/{id}/related or add GET /api/cards/{id}/suggestions. Build one-hop graph over backlinks rows (source_id_int -> target_id_int; JOIN cards for ownership). Return PartialCard + score + reason. Frontend: surface in rail Links tab (own collapsible or sublist of Related Cards).
acceptance_criteria: Suggestions list returns second-degree cards not already linked/referenced, with scores; endpoint respects user ownership.
close_reason: Backend: GET /api/cards/{id}/suggestions (routes/cards.go, handlers/cards.go). services.GetSecondDegreeSuggestions (references.go): first-degree = GetReferences + source's outgoing backlink rows (covers structured-data/test links), then outgoing links of first-degree cards via backlinks with ownership join on targets; scored by co-occurrence count; excludes source, direct references, parent/siblings/children, other users' cards; reason 'referenced by N cards you reference (: titles)' when <=2 sources. Frontend: getCardSuggestions API; RelatedCards gained a title prop (default 'Related Cards'); Suggestions section in the rail Links tab + mobile accordion (reuses RelatedCards rows/chips/+Ref); container fetches + refreshRelatedCards also invalidates suggestions (references drive them). Tests: TestGetCardSuggestions (score 2/1, exclusions incl. source-outgoing-via-table, ownership) + TestGetCardSuggestions_Empty + RelatedCards title test + container/smoke mock updates. Full go test ./... + 942 frontend tests green; tsc/prettier/build clean.

title: Editor-time link suggestions strip
description:
From plan Phase 2.3. In CardEditor/CardBodyTextArea, compute related candidates on debounce while typing; show a slim 'Link these' strip under the editor (reuse CardItem; click inserts [[card_id|title]]).

Reuses getRelatedCards; no new backend work. Scope note: getRelatedCards needs a card ID - EditPage also serves /app/card/new (AppRoutes.tsx:84) with no ID yet, so gate the strip on an existing card only.
acceptance_criteria: Editing an existing card shows live related-card suggestions; clicking one inserts a wiki-link. The strip never appears for new unsaved cards.
close_reason: New EditorLinkSuggestions component (components/cards/EditorLinkSuggestions.tsx) renders a slim 'Link these' strip under CardBodyTextArea in CardEditor. Debounced 600ms related-card lookup (getRelatedCards) keyed on body/title/id; gated to existing cards (newCard or id<=0 -> never renders, no fetch); excludes cards already linked in the unsaved body ([[id]] or [[id|); capped at 5; click inserts [[card_id|title]] appended to the body via setEditingCard; CardItem's inner anchor click swallowed with preventDefault so click inserts rather than navigates; keyboard accessible (Enter/Space). Tests: 5 new (new-card gate, no-id gate, debounce + render, insert on click, already-linked exclusion) using fake timers + act. 940 frontend tests green; tsc/prettier/build clean. No backend changes.

title: Orphan report: cards with no connections
description:
From plan Phase 2.2. List cards with 0 refs in/out, 0 children, and low shared-entity/tag overlap.

Backend: GET /api/cards/orphans. Query backlinks (JOIN cards for ownership; no PK - dedupe manually) + children + card_tags. IMPORTANT: do NOT run the full related-score per card - it triggers a Typesense semantic call per card (handlers/cards.go:1438). Use a cheap entity/tag-overlap-only proxy or precomputed offline score.

Frontend: section on StatsPage or a dedicated Network tab; list with one-click 'find related' deep-link to ViewPage.
acceptance_criteria: Orphan list returns only own-user cards with no references, no children, and low overlap; no per-card Typesense calls.
close_reason: Backend: GET /api/cards/orphans (routes/cards.go, handlers/cards.go) returns the user's cards with no connections. services.GetOrphanCards (references.go) uses only cheap junction queries — no per-card Typesense calls: backlink in/out (self-links ignored, ownership via cards join since backlinks has no user_id), children (parent_id != id, root convention excluded), shared-entity and shared-tag pair self-joins. Frontend: Orphan Cards section on StatsPage (fetch on mount + Refresh button, CardItem rows that deep-link to the card view where related cards/unlinked mentions/backlink tools live, empty-state message, error state). Tests: TestGetOrphanCards handler test covering isolated/leaf-child orphans vs linked, parent, entity-overlap, tag-overlap, and other-user cards. Full go test ./... + 935 frontend tests green; tsc/prettier/build clean.

title: Unlinked mentions: find cards that mention this card without linking it
description:
From plan Phase 2.1. Find cards whose body mentions the source card's card_id (v1: card_id only; title-token matching is noisy) without a [[...]] or legacy [card_id] link.

Backend: GET /api/cards/{id}/unlinked-mentions -> { card, mention_count, context_snippet }[]. SQL LIKE scan on cards.body + regex filter in Go. Exclude already-linked via backlink.ExtractBacklinks (covers both syntaxes, backlink.go:46-63). Ownership: backlinks table has no user_id column/PK - JOIN cards for user filtering (pattern at services/cards.go:444) and dedupe manually. Route via addProtectedRoute in routes/.

Frontend: collapsible 'Unlinked mentions' in rail Links tab + mobile accordion; each row has an 'Add link' button inserting [[card_id]] into the mentioning card. Reuse addBacklinkToCard helper (zettelkasten-front/src/utils/cardActions.ts:168) which inserts + saves + regenerates backlinks - not raw saveExistingCard.
acceptance_criteria: A card whose body mentions another card's card_id without a link appears in Unlinked mentions with snippet; clicking Add link inserts [[card_id]] and removes it from the list. Only own-user cards returned.
close_reason: Backend: GET /api/cards/{id}/unlinked-mentions (handlers/cards.go + routes/cards.go) returns cards whose body mentions the source card_id without linking to it. services.GetUnlinkedMentions (references.go): instr() candidate prefilter, ExtractBacklinks exclusion ([[id]], [[id|label]], legacy [id]), word-boundary regex (QuoteMeta) for precision, mention count + context snippet, sorted by count desc; numeric-only card_ids skipped (too noisy). Ownership via user_id filter. Frontend: UnlinkedMentions component (snippet + count + +Link), rail collapsible in Links tab, mobile accordion; container fetches + addUnlinkedMentionLink action (getCard -> addBacklinkToCard -> local removal + refetch); refreshUnlinkedMentions wired to CardIdDiscovery rename. Tests: 3 Go handler tests (plain/linked/boundary/ownership, numeric skip, 404), 4 component tests, 1 container test; 924 frontend tests + full go test green; prettier/tsc/build clean.

title: Refresh related cards after card edit/save
description:
From plan Phase 1.3. ViewPageContainer.tsx:122 caches relatedCards; reset to null only on id change (:232) and fetched only when viewingCard && relatedCards === null (:249-254). A body save refetches the card but not related cards.

Invalidate/re-fetch related cards when the saved card body/title changes (e.g. after saveExistingCard in ViewPage handleSaveCard, or on container data refresh).
acceptance_criteria: Editing a card's body/title and saving updates the Related Cards section without a full page reload.
close_reason: Related cards now refetch after save: refreshRelatedCards action invalidates the cache (setRelatedCards(null)), the fetch effect depends on relatedCards so it refetches, and both ViewPage save paths (body edit + CardIdDiscovery) call it. Added container test verifying refetch. typecheck/build/tests green.

title: Group related cards by reason in the rail
description: From plan Phase 1.4. When related cards have >1 distinct reason (entities/tags/similarity), group the Related Cards section into small sublists ('Shared entities', 'Shared tags', 'Semantically similar') instead of one flat list. Only when >1 reason present, to avoid clutter. Depends on reasons being surfaced (sibling issue).
acceptance_criteria: Related Cards section groups by top reason when multiple reasons exist; single-reason results stay flat.
close_reason: RelatedCards.tsx now groups cards into 'Shared entities' / 'Shared tags' / 'Semantically similar' sublists when more than one reason category is present (single-category lists stay flat). Cards map to a primary category from their first recognizable reason (backend merge order: entities, tags, similarity), so no client-side reimplementation of scoring weights. Cards with unrecognized reasons fall through to an ungrouped list. Mobile accordion inherits via the shared component. Added 3 grouping tests; 919 frontend tests green; prettier + build OK.

title: Configurable related-cards scoring via env vars
description:
From plan Phase 1.2 (docs/plans/2026-08-09-card-connections-plan.md). Weights are hardcoded in GetRelatedCardsRoute (handlers/cards.go): entity sharedCount*3 (services/cards.go:1364), tag +1, semantic sc.Score*10.0 (handlers/cards.go:1469), top-10 cutoff (handlers/cards.go:1563).

Read RELATED_ENTITY_WEIGHT, RELATED_TAG_WEIGHT, RELATED_SEMANTIC_WEIGHT, RELATED_MAX_RESULTS from env with current values as defaults; apply semantic weight in place of the inline *10.0. Document all four in go-backend/.env.example.
acceptance_criteria: Setting the four RELATED_* vars changes scoring/limit behavior; unset vars keep current defaults; .env.example documents them.
close_reason: RELATED_ENTITY_WEIGHT / RELATED_TAG_WEIGHT / RELATED_SEMANTIC_WEIGHT / RELATED_MAX_RESULTS now read from env with defaults 3/1/10/10 (envFloat/envInt helpers with fallback, handlers/cards.go); semantic scale no longer inline; both .env.example files document them. Fixed pluralization bug in sharedMatchReason ('entitys' -> singular/plural args). Added TestGetRelatedCards_ConfigurableWeights (weight + reason name), TestGetRelatedCards_MaxResultsLimit (3 candidates, cap 2), TestEnvFloatAndEnvInt. Full go test ./... green.

title: Show why cards are related (reasons chips with matched entity/tag names)
description:
From plan Phase 1.1 (docs/plans/2026-08-09-card-connections-plan.md). RelatedCard.Reasons is computed by the backend but never rendered.

Backend: GetCardsBySharedEntities/GetCardsBySharedTags (services/cards.go:1318,1378) return score maps only. Add batched SQL (WHERE card_pk IN (...)) against entity_card_junction and card_tags to collect matched entity/tag NAMES per candidate; change the reasons payload from deduped categories ('entities'/'tags'/'similarity') to include names. Payload shape change: update go-backend/models/card.go comment + zettelkasten-front/src/models/Card.ts RelatedCard.reasons accordingly (backend + frontend model + component must change together).

Frontend: RelatedCards.tsx renders reasons as small chips/labels (e.g. 'Shares 3 entities: Python, LLM', 'tag: research', 'semantic'). ViewMobileLayout inherits automatically.
acceptance_criteria: Related cards in desktop rail and mobile accordion show why each card matched (matched entity/tag names + similarity flag). go test ./... and frontend tests pass.
close_reason: Backend now returns informative reasons ('3 shared entities: Python, LLM', '1 shared tag: research', 'semantically similar') via new SharedMatch{Count,Names} from batched entity/tag name queries (services/cards.go) + sharedMatchReason helper (handlers/cards.go). RelatedCards.tsx renders them as chips in the rail and mobile accordion (shared component). go test ./... green; 916 frontend tests green (6 new for RelatedCards); prettier + gofmt clean; prod build OK.

title: Phase C.2: ui/Popover + ui/Combobox primitives for non-menu popovers (TaskDropdown, CardBodyHelpPopover, QuickTagPopover, BacklinkInputDropdownList)
description:
Why: the z11.15 Menu sweep (closed) routed true menus through ui/Menu but explicitly deferred components that are NOT menus — they are popovers/autocompletes whose semantics a role=menu would corrupt (a11y regression) and whose mechanics (custom triggers, viewport-flip portal positioning, controlled open state, caret anchoring, async search) would need invasive extensions to the Menu primitive. The z11.11 dialog sweep (closed) likewise deferred InlineCardReferenceDialog (same category: anchor-positioned popover with viewport-flip + portal, not a centered modal).

Do:
- Create src/components/ui/Popover.tsx on Headless UI Popover: trigger + panel + positioning + Escape + click-outside, with a triggerClassName replacement escape hatch like ui/Menu gained
- Create src/components/ui/Combobox.tsx on Headless UI Combobox for searchable autocompletes
- Migrate the deferred components:
  - TaskDropdown (reusable wrapper: colored-badge trigger + viewport-flip portal; 4 call sites: TaskStatusDisplay, TaskPriorityDisplay, TaskDateDisplay, TaskReminderDisplay)
  - CardBodyHelpPopover (rich help content — Headless Popover today)
  - QuickTagPopover (caret-anchored autocomplete tied to the title input keyboard events; has its own test)
  - BacklinkInputDropdownList (debounced async semantic search autocomplete rendering CardTag rows)
  - InlineCardReferenceDialog (anchor-positioned card-search popover: viewport-flip + portal + resize handling; used by card editors)
- Vitest spec per primitive; run test:run + format:check + build

Acceptance Criteria:
- ui/Popover + ui/Combobox exist, typed, tested (Vitest spec per primitive)
- All 5 deferred components route through the new primitives; zero hand-rolled popover/autocomplete markup remains in them
- No role=menu semantics on non-menu panels
- test:run, format:check, build green
acceptance_criteria: See acceptance criteria in description
notes: 2026-08-09 implementation: ui/Popover.tsx + ui/Combobox.tsx created (Headless-based, Vitest-tested: 11 tests). Migrated: CardBodyHelpPopover -> ui/Popover; BacklinkInputDropdownList -> ui/Combobox; InlineCardReferenceDialog -> ui/Popover (initialOpen + invisible fixed anchor + portal + onClose notification); TaskDropdown -> ui/Popover (uncontrolled + close render-prop) with all 4 Task*Display surfaces converted (TaskStatusDisplay, TaskPriorityDisplay via TaskDropdown; TaskDateDisplay + TaskReminderDisplay converted from their inline hand-rolled portals to TaskDropdown/ui/Popover) and useTaskDropdown.ts DELETED (dead). DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION — QuickTagPopover NOT migrated: it is a caret-anchored autocomplete with parent-controlled open and NO trigger button; Headless Popover's uncontrolled button-triggered model cannot represent it — its click-outside would close the popover when clicking the title input (the anchor, which must stay clickable), and there is no imperative open. Keeping its own logic (has its own test). Net: 4 of 5 deferred components routed through the new primitives; the 5th documented with rationale.
close_reason: Phase C.2 complete. Primitives: src/components/ui/Popover.tsx (trigger + panel + portal + anchor viewport-flip + initialOpen for programmatic popovers + onClose open->closed notification + triggerClassName/panelStyle escape hatches; NOT role=menu — popovers are not menus) and src/components/ui/Combobox.tsx (searchable autocomplete: input + options list + keyboard nav, caller owns query/ranking) with Vitest specs (11 tests: opens/closes/Escape+focus-return/title/triggerClassName/close render-prop/initialOpen for Popover; type-to-open/select/keyboard-nav/loading/empty for Combobox). Migrated 4 of 5 deferred components: CardBodyHelpPopover -> ui/Popover (side-anchored panel); BacklinkInputDropdownList -> ui/Combobox (all 11 call sites unchanged — debounce/API/ranking stays in the component); InlineCardReferenceDialog -> ui/Popover (invisible fixed trigger at the anchor + initialOpen + portal + anchor flip; deleted ~180 lines of manual viewport-flip/click-outside/resize logic; floating-ui handles repositioning); TaskDropdown -> ui/Popover (uncontrolled + close render-prop) and ALL FOUR Task*Display surfaces converted to the shared machinery — TaskStatusDisplay + TaskPriorityDisplay via TaskDropdown, TaskDateDisplay + TaskReminderDisplay converted from their own hand-rolled portals (each had duplicate badge/positioning/click-outside/Escape code) to TaskDropdown/ui/Popover; useTaskDropdown.ts DELETED (zero users). DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION — QuickTagPopover kept as-is: caret-anchored autocomplete with parent-controlled open and no trigger button; Headless Popover's uncontrolled button-triggered model can't represent it (click-outside would fire on the title-input anchor; no imperative open). Its own test still passes. Gates: test:run 909 pass (11 new primitive tests), format:check clean, tsc clean, build OK, check:primitives pass.

title: FileVault: wire Typesense files indexing (init/upload/edit/delete) so search path is reachable
description:
## Context
Code review of the 72f FileVault fixes found that the Typesense files search path is unwired: InitFilesCollection, IndexFileInTypesense, and DeleteFileFromTypesense (go-backend/handlers/files_typesense.go) have zero call sites in the repo. The 'files' collection is never created (bootstrap/typesense.go only creates the card/entity collections), nothing indexes files on upload or metadata edit, and nothing de-indexes on delete. As a result every GetAllFilesRoute search with Typesense enabled fails against the missing collection and silently falls back to SQL — the 72f.2/72f.3 Typesense fixes (card population, filters, sort, quota) are latent until this is wired.

## Problem
- No InitFilesCollection call at server startup
- UploadFileRoute / EditFileMetadataRoute never call IndexFileInTypesense (descriptions, tags, extracted_text changes are never re-indexed)
- DeleteFileRoute never calls DeleteFileFromTypesense (soft-deleted files stay in the index)
- The text-extraction job (JobTypeFileTextExtraction in services/llmprocessor.go) is a placeholder, so extracted_text is never populated for indexing

## Acceptance Criteria
- Files collection created at startup when Typesense is enabled
- Upload indexes the file; metadata edits (name/description/card_pk/tags) re-index; delete de-indexes
- Soft-deleted files never surface in Typesense results (native path already filters is_deleted, but stale index entries must be cleaned on delete)
- Manual verify: with Typesense enabled, search matches file contents/descriptions and the 72f.2/72f.3 paths run for real

## Non-Goals
- Full text extraction pipeline (separate concern; extracted_text placeholder noted)
close_reason: Implemented: InitFilesCollection (+ backfill of existing files) called at startup alongside InitSearchCollection; IndexFileInTypesense on upload, metadata edit (name/description/card_pk), tag add/remove; DeleteFileFromTypesense on delete. All calls nil-client-guarded + non-fatal (search falls back to SQL). Also fixed pre-existing TagFileRoute testing hazard (unconditional Commit/deferred Rollback on the shared test tx → now ShouldCommitTx-guarded, matching entity.go pattern). Tests: new TagFileRoute/UntagFileRoute route tests; existing upload/edit/delete tests cover no-regression. Manual verify pending (needs a live Typesense).

title: FileVault: text/markdown preview and content search snippets using extracted_text
description:
## Context
The backend already extracts text from uploads (JobTypeFileTextExtraction -> files.extracted_text) and Typesense indexes it (QueryBy name,description,extracted_text,tags), so search already matches file CONTENTS — but the UI gives no evidence: FileRender shows 'Preview not available' for text/markdown, and search results have no snippets/highlighting. For a knowledge-management vault this is the highest-value addition: users should be able to search inside documents and see where the match is.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Text/markdown/code files preview in FileRender (fetch extracted_text or render the downloaded blob as text)
- Search results show a snippet around the match (Typesense highlights, or frontend extracts from extracted_text) and the matching field (name/content/tag)
- Preview modal for text files includes copy/download affordances
- Tests: FileRender text path renders content; snippet helper tested
close_reason: Implemented: inline text extraction on upload populates extracted_text (job was a placeholder); search results include extracted_text + server-computed snippet/snippet_field (name/description/content/tag); FileRender previews text/markdown (react-markdown or pre) with Copy + Download; FileListItem shows the snippet with a field badge. Tests: Go snippet/extraction helpers, upload extraction, runFileListQuery snippet paths; TS FileRender text/markdown/copy/non-text + FileListItem snippet.

title: FileVault: filter files by tag
description:
## Context
File tags are fully implemented (models.File.tags, getFileTags/createFileTag/tagFile/untagFile API, FileMetadataEditor, Typesense facet 'tags') but the FileVault has no way to filter the list by tag. This is the most obvious KMS gap — tags are the primary organization mechanism and they're invisible in the vault.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tag filter control in FileVault (chips or dropdown populated from getFileTags, with file counts if available)
- Selecting a tag narrows the list to files with that tag; combinable with existing search/filetype/unlinked filters
- Backend: tag filter param on GET /files (SQL: EXISTS join on files_tags; Typesense: filter_by tags:=tag)
- Tag state survives pagination; Clear-all resets it; tests for both SQL and Typesense paths
close_reason: Implemented: tag filter param on GET /files (SQL EXISTS join on files_tags; Typesense filter_by tags:=tag via buildTypesenseFilterBy); FileVault tag chips populated from getFileTags with file counts, toggle on/off, composable with search/filetype/unlinked, survives pagination, Clear-all resets. Tests: SQL tag filter + unknown tag + filter composition; buildTypesenseFilterBy; smoke test chip render/click/clear.

title: FileVault: keyboard navigation broken — Enter no-op, Delete uses stale closure + whole selection
description:
## Context
FileVault.tsx implements arrow/j/k highlight navigation with Enter and Delete actions.

- Enter: queries `[data-file-id]` and calls .click() — but that attribute is on the <li> (line ~950), which has no click handler, so Enter does nothing despite the 'Trigger the file preview' comment.
- Delete: calls handleBulkDelete(), which deletes ALL selected files (or nothing when nothing is selected) rather than the highlighted row. Also handleKeyDown's useCallback deps omit selectedFiles/handleBulkDelete, so it holds a stale closure — pressing Delete right after selecting files can act on an outdated selection set.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open FileVault with files; arrow down to highlight a row; press Enter — nothing happens
2. Highlight a row without selecting it; press Delete — nothing happens (confusing; highlight implies intent)
3. Select files, then Delete — deletes may use stale selection depending on render timing

- Delete on highlighted row deletes just that row with confirmation (or documented intent to delete selection)
- handleKeyDown deps include everything used (no stale closures); tests cover highlight + Enter/Delete
close_reason: Fixed: filetype: syntax parsed into filetype param (util + tests); keyboard Enter clicks real download link, Delete removes highlighted row with confirm, no stale closures (tests); uploads preserve current query; single fetch effect (mount-call-count asserted in smoke test)

title: FileVault: documented filetype: search syntax always returns zero results
description:
## Context
The FileVault search help popup documents `filetype:TYPE` syntax, and clicking a file's type chip (FileListItem.tsx:125) sets the search box to `filetype:image/png` (etc). No backend path handles this syntax.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open FileVault, click a file's filetype chip (e.g. image/png) OR type `filetype:pdf` in the search box
2. Result: zero files match
- SQL fallback: `f.name LIKE '%filetype:pdf%' OR f.type LIKE '%filetype:pdf%'` matches nothing
- Typesense: the whole string is passed as Q against name/description/extracted_text/tags — literal 'filetype:pdf' matches nothing

The backend has a dedicated `filetype` query param that this syntax never feeds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `filetype:<type>` in the search box filters by file type (frontend parses it into the filetype param, or backend parses the syntax)
- Clicking a file's type chip produces a non-empty filtered list
- Help text matches actual behavior
close_reason: Fixed: filetype: syntax parsed into filetype param (util + tests); keyboard Enter clicks real download link, Delete removes highlighted row with confirm, no stale closures (tests); uploads preserve current query; single fetch effect (mount-call-count asserted in smoke test)

title: FileVault: Typesense search path ignores filetype/unlinked/sort filters and drops storage quota + description
description:
## Context
GetAllFilesRoute short-circuits to searchFilesInTypesense whenever Typesense is available and a search term exists. That path only filters by user_id and always sorts by _text_match,created_at — the filetypeFilter, unlinkedOnly, and sort/order params are silently ignored. Its response also omits storage_used/max_storage (storage bar disappears) and description/extracted_text.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Typesense enabled; upload a file; give it a description; link a file to a card
2. Search so Typesense path is taken, with the 'Unlinked Only' toggle on, a filetype chip selected, and sort=Name
3. Unlinked/filetype filters and sort have no effect; storage quota bar disappears from the UI (max_storage=0)
4. Open Edit Details on a search result: description shows empty even when set

## Acceptance Criteria
- Typesense search path honors filetype, unlinked, sort, and order params (filter_by/sort_by)
- Typesense response includes storage_used + max_storage (or the SQL path computes them after Typesense hits)
- Search results include description (and card, see sibling bug) so the editor shows real values
- Tests cover Typesense path with filters applied
close_reason: Fixed: Typesense path now honors filetype/unlinked/sort/order (native sort_by for plain searches; candidate-ID + shared SQL filtering for filtered searches), returns storage_used/max_storage, and search results use the frontend filetype key with card+description (tests: runFileListQuery candidate sets, unlinked/filetype SQL filters, buildTypesenseSortBy)

title: E2E smoke.sh: cargo build failure is swallowed by '|| true' — stale binary can pass the smoke
description:
Code review of Zettelgarden-77j (desktop E2E smoke) found desktop/e2e/smoke.sh:58 does 'cargo build --release ... 2>&1 | tail -5 || true'. With set -euo pipefail the pipeline failure is masked, and the later '[ -x APP_BIN ]' check passes if a STALE release binary exists from an earlier build. A broken build would silently run the old binary and the smoke would green — false confidence from a harness whose purpose is verifying the shipped binary.

Fix: make the build fatal on failure (tail the log then exit 1), or verify the binary is newer than the sources (mtime compare / checksum) before running.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build failure in smoke.sh aborts the run with the build log shown; a stale binary cannot pass the smoke
