Goal: a typed, tested src/components/ui/ primitives layer (Button, Modal, ConfirmDialog, Menu/Dropdown, Badge, Spinner, Field/Input/Select/Label) that components are required to use, then mechanical migration of existing surfaces. Consistent look + single place to change each primitive — NOT a UI redesign. Visual changes minimal except where shared Modal/Button intentionally unify look. Deliberate a11y improvement: raw dialogs gain focus-trap/aria/Escape via Headless-based Modal (behavior change — add e2e/smoke.ts to quality gates).

Phased (each independently shippable, ordered by leverage):
- Phase A: define primitives (foundation) — Button+danger variant, Modal, ConfirmDialog (+ fix useConfirmDialog cancel-path bug), Menu/Dropdown, Badge, Spinner, form primitives, single primary color decision + docs page.
- Phase B: seed adoption on highest-traffic surfaces — button surfaces (CardListItem, TaskListItem, EditPageHeader, ViewPageHeader), all confirm flows -> shared ConfirmDialog.
- Phase C: sweep remaining components — dialog shells -> Modal (incl. inline fixed inset-0 shells in EntityPage/FactPage/SchemaPage/ViewPageContainer/AdminPage/FileVault), menus -> Menu, status pills -> Badge, spinners -> Spinner, form fields -> Field/Input; delete dead code (admin/ConfirmDialog, AdminTopBar, admin/StatusBadge) + superseded implementations.
- Phase D: governance — no fixed inset-0 outside ui/ (grep/CI check; ESLint is greenfield, treat as follow-up), doc convention, optional palette normalization in tailwind.config.js.

Coordinate: Zettelgarden-h98 (prune dead frontend code) lists different files but touches similar delete-file territory — sequence/split so both land cleanly. Quality gates after each phase: npm run test:run, format:check, build, e2e/smoke.ts.

Success Criteria:
- src/components/ui/* primitives exist, typed, tested (Vitest spec per primitive)
- No new raw fixed inset-0 modal shells; all existing migrated (incl. inline shells)
- One ConfirmDialog API across tasks/admin/rss/tabs; useConfirmDialog cancel path resolves (no hanging await)
- One Badge in use; StatusBadge/JobStatusBadge removed
- No hand-rolled spinner markup remaining (SVG, border-div, or unicode)
- Single primary button color (brand) in use; danger variant exists
- Dead code removed: admin/ConfirmDialog, AdminTopBar, admin/StatusBadge
- Governance check in place: no fixed inset-0 outside ui/
- npm run test:run, format:check, build, e2e/smoke.ts green
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE — all 16 child issues closed (A-D). Primitives layer exists and is tested: ui/Button (danger variant), ui/Modal, ui/ConfirmDialog (+useConfirmDialog cancel-path fix), ui/Menu + ui/Dropdown, ui/Badge, ui/Spinner, ui/Field/Input/Select/Label; single primary color bg-palette-dark documented. Migrations landed: button surfaces (EditPageHeader, ViewPageHeader), all confirm flows -> ConfirmDialog, ALL 26 dialog shells -> ui/Modal (24 migrated in z11.11 + RollbackConfirmDialog already primitive + InlineCardReferenceDialog deferred to 12g), menus -> ui/Menu (13 listed: 5 dead deleted, 4 migrated, 4 non-menus deferred to 12g), badges/spinners swept, dead code deleted (admin/ConfirmDialog, AdminTopBar, admin/StatusBadge), palette normalized (modern.* retired, ToggleSlider Tailwind-ified). Governance: npm run check:primitives fails on raw modal shells / Headless Dialog outside ui/ (passes on migrated codebase; allowlist for FileVault overlays). Gates green throughout: test:run 898, format:check clean, tsc clean, build OK. FOLLOW-UPS (tracked): Zettelgarden-12g (Phase C.2: ui/Popover + ui/Combobox primitives for TaskDropdown, CardBodyHelpPopover, QuickTagPopover, BacklinkInputDropdownList, InlineCardReferenceDialog), Zettelgarden-9ky (ESLint introduction).

title: FileVault: Typesense search ignores active filetype filter
description: When both a search term and a filetype filter are active (e.g. searching while 'Documents' chip selected), GetAllFilesRoute short-circuits to searchFilesInTypesense, which never receives the filetype param — so results are returned unfiltered by type. Pass filetypeFilter through to the Typesense search (add a facet filter f.type LIKE the filetype pattern, mirroring the SQL path) or fall through to SQL when a filetype filter is set. Found while fixing the files:null crash (commit 441487b6).
close_reason: Fixed by 72f.3 (commit db6ba437): searchFilesInTypesense now takes filetypeFilter; with a filter active it collects candidate IDs from Typesense and narrows via runFileListQuery (f.type LIKE), so search + filetype chip no longer returns unfiltered results

title: Migrate retention-days + OIDC auto-provision into admin settings; make mail_enabled hot-reloadable
description:
Review of the admin settings page (6er.15) found config still stuck in env that belongs in the admin-managed config.yaml, plus a hot-reload bug.

Scope:
1. Expose oidc_auto_provision in the admin settings UI — it is already in the settings registry, the public /api/settings payload, and frontend AppSettings, but the admin page/form/TS type omit it, so operators must hand-edit config.yaml to close OIDC auto-provisioning.

Run the desktop app (desktop/ + a live Go backend): create/edit/delete a card and a task with the network disconnected (mirror + outbox), reconnect, and confirm reconciliation; verify the sidebar sync indicator shows pending/offline states and the app opens instantly offline with the keychain session preserved. Also verify the first-run bootstrap path (fresh mirror, no token).
close_reason:
Desktop E2E smoke built and PASSING end-to-end: desktop/e2e/smoke.sh boots a live Go backend + release Tauri binary (custom-protocol, embedded dist) under xvfb and drives a scripted scenario inside the real webview via an env-gated bridge (ZG_E2E=1, never injected in normal runs). Scenarios verified: (fresh) register + real login form -> fresh-mirror bootstrap through the real IPC -> online create+sync -> OFFLINE create/edit/delete of a card and create/edit of a task with ZERO window.fetch calls on the hot path (indicator shows Offline · N pending) -> reconnect + reconciliation (server spot-check) -> Synced; (session) relaunch with the same app data dir + keychain boots authenticated and renders the offline-created card instantly.

The smoke caught five real defects, all fixed and committed: (1) keyring='3' enabled no store features and silently used an in-memory mock — tokens lost every restart; now real Secret Service/Keychain/Credential Manager + opt-in ZG_KEYCHAIN_FILE for headless; (2) backend CORS allowed only its own origin, so the tauri://localhost shell could not reach any server; (3) LoginPage navigated before auth settled, bouncing MainApp back to /login (latent web bug); (4) sync transport double-prefixed /api; (5) engine's terminal progress event left the indicator stuck on 'Syncing…'. title: Removing a schema from a card returns 400 'structured_data requires schema_id'
description:
Found in code review of Zettelgarden-s2l (required schema fields, 2026-08-08). User-visible bug in the schema-removal path, pre-existing (check predates s2l) but adjacent to the refactored code.

## Reproduction (code trace)
1. Card has a schema attached (schema_id set, structured_data filled).
2. User opens the card editor and clears the schema dropdown (CardSchemaSection.handleSchemaChange -> onSchemaChange(null) + onDataChange({})).
3. Save sends schema_id: null with structured_data: {} (empty object, 2 bytes).
4. REST handler (handlers/cards.go UpdateCardRoute + CreateCardRoute) hits the else-if branch: params.StructuredData != nil && len(*params.StructuredData) > 0 -> {} is len 2 > 0 -> 400 "structured_data requires schema_id to be specified".

So detaching a schema from a card cannot be saved via the UI. Also affects CreateCardRoute for the same payload shape.

## Fix direction
- Treat an EMPTY structured_data object ({ } or empty) as "no structured data" in the else-if guard (e.g. unmarshal and check len(map) == 0, or compare to "{}").
- Alternatively, decide schema removal clears structured_data to null server-side when schema_id is null.
- Verify both create and update paths, plus the sync push path (sync currently accepts structured_data-without-schema_id silently; see sibling follow-up bead).

## Acceptance
Clearing a schema in the editor and saving succeeds (200), structured_data is cleared / not persisted; re-attaching a different schema works; creating a card with non-empty structured_data but no schema still returns the 400 (that contract is intentional for stray data); handler tests cover detach-with-{} and detach-with-null.
notes:
Fixed 2026-08-08. Root cause: the REST guard used byte-length (len(*params.StructuredData) > 0) so an empty {} (2 bytes) was treated as non-empty structured data, and UpdateCard's preserve-branch kept the old schema when both fields were nil — so the editor's detach payload (schema_id: null + structured_data: {}) could never detach.

Fix (backend only):
- services/schema_validation.go: new StructuredDataIsEmpty(raw) helper — true for nil, JSON null, empty object/array (semantic emptiness, not byte length).
- handlers/cards.go: both UpdateCardRoute and CreateCardRoute now (a) read the body once and unmarshal, (b) call normalizeSchemaDetach which detects an EXPLICIT schema_id:null in the raw body (distinct from a partial update that omits the field) and, when structured_data is empty, sets ClearSchema + nils StructuredData, and (c) the stray-data guard now uses StructuredDataIsEmpty so {} passes while non-empty data without schema still 400s.
- Sync push path untouched (divergence is tracked in sibling bead a1u).

Tests added (handlers/cards_test.go): detach-with-{} (200, schema_id + structured_data cleared), detach-with-null (200, cleared), omitted-schema-fields partial update preserves association (regression guard), update-path stray data still 400, create-path {} payload succeeds with no schema, create-path non-empty stray data still 400. Full go test ./... green.
close_reason: Detach payload (schema_id: null + structured_data: {} / null) now saves with 200 and clears the association; non-empty stray data without schema still 400s. 6 new handler tests; go test ./... green.

title: Sync push does not enforce card_id uniqueness that REST enforces
description: Code-review follow-up (P2-3): the REST write paths check card_id uniqueness (checkIsCardIDUnique / UpdateCard), but the sync push apply path (services/sync_apply.go applyCardUpsert) inserts cards with no uniqueness check. Two offline devices creating the same card_id both land server-side; duplicate card_id corrupts GetPartialCardByCardID (parent resolution returns the first match, ambiguous), GetBacklinks (target keyed by card_id string) and GetNextRootCardID. Needs a design decision: LWW-reject duplicates on push (conflict + lost edit for the loser), or accept and document (schema has no UNIQUE on card_id by design).
close_reason: Fixed in 8ba5aa9d. idp: applyCardUpsert now mirrors REST's checkIsCardIDUnique — CREATE-path duplicate card_id is MERGED onto the winner (adopt the winner's uuid, like the tag name-merge, so no ghost row re-conflicts on every edit); UPDATE-path rename to an owned card_id is a conflict (lost edit). Empty card_id exempt. merged() helper generalized to take the collection. dsd: retryMatchesCurrent relaxed to payload-match-only (no version==base+1 guard) — identical content is idempotent-applied even when the row advanced past base+1; genuinely different stale content still conflicts. Tests: TestSyncPushRejectsDuplicateCardID + TestSyncPushIdenticalContentStaleBaseNoConflict. Gates: go test ./... green, sync-engine 40/40, harness 9/9.

title: Enforce required schema fields on card save (UI makes the promise, backend doesn't keep it)
description:
Schema assessment (2026-08-08, SchemaPage.tsx review): FieldDefinition.required is fully supported in the editor (StructuredDataEditor renders '*' + '(required)' labels) and in the field editor (SchemaDialog marks fields required), but there is NO validation preventing a card from being saved with missing required structured data.

## Where the gap lives
- Frontend: components/schemas/StructuredDataEditor.tsx marks required fields but never blocks save; components/schemas/EditableCell.tsx (table inline edit) calls saveExistingCard with no required check; EditPage.tsx CardSchemaSection has no validation hook.
- Backend: handlers/cards.go save path (saveNewCard/saveExistingCard) — verify whether schema required fields are validated server-side (likely not; structured_data is stored as-is). The schema definition is server-side truth (models/schema.go FieldDefinition.Required), so the backend should enforce it.

## Do
1. Backend: on card save with card_schema_id set, validate that every required field is present (non-empty; for select/multi-select, valid option? at least non-empty) in structured_data. Return a clear 4xx error naming the missing field(s).
2. Frontend: mirror the validation before save in EditPage (CardSchemaSection / StructuredDataEditor) and in EditableCell (table inline edit) so users get inline feedback, not a server error.
3. Tests: handler test (save card missing required field -> 4xx + message; save with all required -> ok), frontend test for the inline validation if cheap.

## Scope boundary
- Empty vs invalid option values: for v1, require non-empty presence only (empty string / null / undefined = missing). Option-whitelist validation (select must be one of the options) is a follow-up decision, note it in the issue if skipped.
- Defer: required enforcement on the {{schema:}} markdown embed render path (read-only view should still render, maybe with an 'incomplete' badge — optional).
acceptance_criteria: Saving a card with a required schema field missing/empty fails with a clear message naming the field, both via REST (Go handler test) and from the edit page inline (frontend); saving with all required fields present succeeds; EditableCell table edit respects the same rule; full Go + frontend suites green.
close_reason: Implemented. Backend: ValidateStructuredData now treats empty/whitespace strings and empty arrays as missing for required fields (isEmptyRequiredValue); shared ValidateCardStructuredData helper used by both REST create/update (deduped the duplicated handler blocks) AND the sync push path (applyCardUpsert) so a pushed card with a schema but missing/empty required structured_data is refused with 400 + message naming the field (ValidationError -> 400 in PushRoute). Frontend: getMissingRequiredFields/isEmptyValue util (utils/schemaValidation.ts) used by EditPage handleSaveCard (inline 'Please fill required field(s): ...' before save) and EditableCell (required fields cannot be emptied + server error message surfaced). Tests: services empty-string/whitespace/null/empty-array + zero/false-accepted cases; handler TestCreateCardWithSchema_MissingRequiredField now asserts 400 + message (was documenting old behavior), TestCreateCardWithSchema_EmptyRequiredField; sync TestSyncPushSchemaValidationRejectsInvalidStructuredData (valid applied, missing/empty -> 400); 6 frontend util tests. Full Go suite + 766 frontend tests green at commit time. NOTE: Go changes were swept into parallel-session commit d6ce3b87 (a5q.6 message) mid-session; frontend committed separately ebdf3d69. Post-commit tree was mid-c1x (memory removal) by parallel session - unrelated.

## Cleanup complete — feature removed (option a)

Commit `9151da93`. The half-implemented AI-agent multi-user feature is **removed**. No agent handlers/routes ever shipped, so this was dead weight: always-empty tables, always-NULL columns, and an unused agent API-key auth path.

### Removed
- **Schema** (`go-backend/schema/sqlite/schema.sqlite.sql`, fresh builds): `agent_activity_log` table + 3 indexes; `cards.created_by_agent_id` + index; `users.is_agent`/`owner_user_id`/`api_key_hash` + CHECK constraints + FK + 2 indexes.

- **Existing DBs**: idempotent boot migration in `ensureSQLiteSchemaUpgrades` (server/database.go) — drops the table/indexes and rebuilds `users` + `cards` without the agent columns (SQLite can't DROP COLUMN past CHECK/FK constraints; `sqliteRebuildTable` runs the 12-step rebuild with foreign_keys toggled on a single connection, in a transaction). Runs once, guarded by column existence.

### Kept
- **API keys** (`api_keys` table, handlers/api_keys.go, frontend `apiKeys.ts`/`APIKeysManagement.tsx`) — that is the general user-API-keys feature, unrelated to agents.
- Archived Postgres migrations 0138–0141 (historical record, under `schema/archive/postgres/`).

### Verified
- `go build ./...`, `go vet` (only pre-existing oauth.go warnings), full `go test ./...` green.
- New regression test `TestEnsureSQLiteSchemaUpgrades_DropsAgentRemnants` — simulates a pre-thw DB, asserts columns/table/indexes dropped, data preserved, non-agent indexes recreated, idempotent second run, FKs still enforced.

| zettelkasten-front/src/components/layout/IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md | ARCHIVE | → docs/archive/reports/MobileTopBar_IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md (one-off). QUICK_START.md + README.md kept (component docs). |
| desktop/README.md, zg/README.md, zettelgarden-mcp/README.md | KEEP | Current. |
| sync-engine/ (no README) | ADD | Created sync-engine/README.md (new module had zero docs). |
| python-mail/ (dir) | DELETE | Untracked leftover (mail.log + __pycache__); python-mail converted to Go in 6er.12. Removed. |
| docs/archive/README.md | ADD | Archive index explaining the archive + per-file rationale. |

### Acceptance checks
- Inventory table recorded ✓ (above)
- No one-off report/summary at repo root or module roots ✓
- README + CLAUDE.md describe current app (SQLite, local storage, self-hosted, Tauri, Go mail) ✓
- No current-state doc references removed features (mailing list, blog, landing page, user memory, python-mail, Postgres-as-live, B2-as-live, Electron shell) ✓ — verified by grep; remaining mentions are in labeled historical docs or accurate "retired/archived" statements
- Historical plans carry SUPERSEDED/historical label ✓ (23 plans; 3 intentional exclusions)
- All internal doc links resolve ✓ (checked per-file across README/CLAUDE/AGENTS/runbooks/module READMEs)

### Notes / follow-ups
- Memory feature: still disabled-but-present in code (c1x tracks full removal). Removed its CLAUDE.md feature bullet. go-backend/prompts/card_memory_assistant.md + memory tools remain as c1x scope.
- AI-agent multi-user (TODO.md): never completed; agent tables exist in SQLite schema but no handlers/routes. Flagged for a decision (finish vs remove) — not part of this docs issue.

title: Sync test coverage gaps: retry idempotency (update/delete), multi-user isolation, feed pagination, engine vs real SQLite adapter
description:
Found in code review of v5b (tsv/nqx/13d). Current gaps that let the v5b.1/v5b.2 bugs ship unnoticed:

- No handler test for update/delete retry idempotency (the existing TestSyncPushIdempotentRetry only covers the create/base-0 path).
- No multi-user isolation test: user A's snapshot cursor / changes feed must never expose or skip user B's rows (the cursor is a global sync_log max - correct by construction, but untested).
- No pagination test for the changes feed past syncFeedPageSize (500).
- All 11 engine tests run against InMemoryAdapter; the real SqliteStorageAdapter gets only 5 adapter-level tests, so adapter divergence (see v5b.2) is untested. Add engine-level scenarios against the SQLite adapter (offline gap, retry, delete-then-recreate, tag merge).,
acceptance_criteria: New tests: handler update-retry and delete-retry (idempotent, 0 lost edits); handler multi-user cursor/feed isolation; handler feed pagination >500 rows; engine scenarios against SqliteStorageAdapter (offline gap, dropped-response retry, delete-then-recreate, tag merge). All suites green.
close_reason: Added TestSyncMultiUserIsolation (snapshot/feed isolation both directions, global cursor skips nothing), TestSyncFeedPagination (501 rows page at 500 with stable cursor/hasMore), and engine-sqlite.test.ts running offline gap, dropped-response retry, delete-then-recreate, and tag-merge against the real SqliteStorageAdapter. Update/delete retry idempotency already covered in v5b.1. vitest 27/27 + go test ./... green; landed 6134e08d.

title: sync_log has no retention/pruning policy (unbounded growth)
description:
Found in code review of v5b (13d). The Phase 0a description specified retention ('append-only, never pruned while a client cursor trails; retention = keep rows >= N days past oldest active cursor, else force re-bootstrap') but no pruning/retention logic exists anywhere, and there is no client-cursor registration to even compute 'oldest active cursor'. services/sync.go's comment claims the escape hatch without implementing it.

Every card/task/tag mutation appends a sync_log row forever - unbounded growth on any long-running instance, and the changes feed scans with id > since per user.

Fix direction: pick a policy (e.g. prune rows older than N days past the oldest known client cursor, tracked via a lightweight cursor heartbeat endpoint or client-reported cursor on push), or explicitly defer + document for the hosted rollout. Do NOT prune while Phase 1b/2b clients are still mid-work.,
acceptance_criteria: A documented, implemented retention policy: sync_log rows older than the threshold are pruned only when no client cursor trails them; clients with stale cursors are force-re-bootstrapped (snapshot). A Go test proves pruning + re-bootstrap behavior. Policy chosen before the hosted rollout.
close_reason: Implemented + documented the retention policy: rows older than 30 days AND at/below the oldest ACTIVE client cursor are pruned; clients report their cursor on push (SyncPushRequest.Cursor) into the new sync_clients heartbeat (schema + boot self-heal); a device that stopped reporting no longer blocks pruning; a returning stale client gets reset=true from the changes feed and re-bootstraps via snapshot (engine pull re-bootstraps, outbox survives). Go tests prove pruning + dead-device exclusion + feed reset; vitest proves engine re-bootstrap. Policy documented in the design doc. go test ./... + vitest 28/28 green; landed 1e759b96.

title: Sync applyCardDelete diverges from DeleteCard: no child/backlink guard, no fact/junction cleanup
description:
Found in code review of v5b (tsv). The UI delete path (services.DeleteCard) refuses deletion when the card has backlinks or children, and cascades cleanup of facts, fact_card_junction and entity_card_junction before soft-deleting. The sync push path (applyCardDelete) soft-deletes unconditionally and performs no such cleanup.

Consequences: a card deleted from a sync client leaves children with dangling parent_id into a soft-deleted card, and derived fact/junction data survives for a deleted card. Same user intent, different outcome by transport.

Fix direction: mirror DeleteCard's guards (conflict-reject or refuse when protected) and run the same fact/junction cleanup, or explicitly document and accept the divergence. Note: the 'card has backlinks' refusal also applies to the normal REST delete; sync delete should behave consistently.,
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a card with children or backlinks via /api/sync/push is refused (or conflict-rejected) matching the REST delete; deleting a normal card via push cleans up facts/junctions exactly as DeleteCard does; handler tests cover both. Go tests green.
close_reason: applyCardDelete now conflict-rejects cards with children or backlinks (matching REST DeleteCard guards; client adopts the surviving row) and runs the shared cleanupCardDerivedData (facts, fact_card_junction, entity_card_junction) extracted from DeleteCard — identical state by either transport. Handler tests: refused-with-children, refused-with-backlinks, cleanup-on-delete. go test ./... green; landed 45041704.

title: Sync push swallows emit failures: mutation commits with no feed entry, push reports applied
description: Found in code review of v5b (tsv). pushContext.emit (services/sync_apply.go) logs a failed sync_log insert and continues; the row write has already happened in the same tx, so the mutation lands on the server but no feed entry is recorded and the push result reports applied. Other clients never see the change.\n\nThis contradicts the Phase 0a invariant documented in services/sync.go ('a failed emit means the mutation is invisible to sync, so callers must propagate the error') - every other write path returns the error, but the push path swallows it. Since the push runs in one transaction, an emit failure is a real DB problem and should roll back the whole batch (or at minimum mark the affected change ignored, never applied).,
acceptance_criteria: A simulated emit failure inside a push rolls back the batch (no partial row writes committed) or the affected change is reported ignored, never applied; Go test covers the failure injection. Go tests green.
close_reason: pushContext.emit now returns the sync_log error and all six apply* paths thread it to ApplySyncPush, which aborts the transaction (PushRoute already rolls back + 500s). A push mutation can no longer commit with no feed entry while reporting applied — Phase 0a invariant honored. Test: drop sync_log mid-batch -> error propagated, partial card write rolled back. go test ./... green; landed 9c5fe481.

title: Sync push: delete-then-recreate of same row can lose the recreate; InMemory adapter coalescing diverges from SQLite
description:
Found in code review of v5b (tsv/nqx). Two related defects:

1) Server side (defensive): a batch containing BOTH a delete and an upsert for the same row_uuid ends with the row soft-deleted and the recreate rejected as a stale conflict (verified by probe: after [delete base1, upsert base1], row is_deleted=true title=v1). The apply loop has no batch-internal tombstone tracking.

2) StorageAdapter divergence: SqliteStorageAdapter.enqueue preserves the ORIGINAL base_version when coalescing a pending entry (LWW-correct); InMemoryAdapter.enqueue replaces the whole entry including baseVersion. In the delete-then-recreate case this yields base 0 for the recreate (row was dropped locally), which the server's BaseVersion==0 shortcut misreads as an idempotent create-retry and does NOT write - silent divergence, and the client reconcile keeps its own data with no pending entry left to correct it. All 11 engine tests run on InMemory, so this path is untested; any future adapter (e.g. Phase 4 web/IndexedDB) copying the InMemory pattern inherits the data loss.

Fix direction: make enqueue base-preserving in BOTH adapters (add a test asserting the coalesced entry keeps the original base); on the server, track batch-internal deletes so a same-batch upsert of the same row_uuid resurrects the row (or treat as create).,
acceptance_criteria: Delete then re-create the same row_uuid in one outbox batch converges: the row is active with the recreate's data on server and all clients. Coalescing keeps the original base_version in both InMemory and SQLite adapters (unit test). Engine test covers delete-then-recreate offline. Go tests + vitest green.
close_reason: Client: InMemoryAdapter.enqueue keeps the original base_version when coalescing (matches SqliteStorageAdapter), so offline delete-then-recreate pushes base 1 and the server applies the recreate instead of dropping it via the base==0 create-retry shortcut. Server: pushContext.deletedInBatch resurrects same-batch deletes on upsert (writes through shortcut+stale checks, re-increments user_stats; tags name-merge path guarded, monotonic version). MockServer mirrors tombstone semantics + is_deleted payload handling. Tests: Go batch delete-then-recreate handler test, InMemory+SQLite coalescing unit tests, engine offline delete-then-recreate convergence test. go test ./... + 21 vitest green; landed addacfbb.

title: Smoke tests for high-risk pages (Dashboard, Search, View, FileVault, Inbox, UserSettings, Entity, Fact)
description:
Why: the largest, most change-prone pages have zero crash-guard. At 0% coverage: FileVault.tsx (872 lines, 44 hooks), NotificationInboxPage.tsx (849, 45 hooks), EntityPage.tsx (525), FactPage.tsx (426), UserSettings.tsx (430), SearchPage.tsx (362), ViewPage.tsx (222), DashboardPage.tsx (230), MemoryPage.tsx (146). These are the files where a refactor can silently break the render path and nothing will catch it.

Do:
- Render-with-providers smoke tests (existing renderWithProviders in src/tests/utils.tsx) for the above pages: mount with realistic mocked data, assert key content renders and the page doesn't throw
- Per-test explicit fetch mocks / shared fixtures — do NOT rely on the global catch-all mock (see a5q.5); build on whatever shared handlers a5q.5 extracts
- Depth of assertion: render + key content present + primary interaction (e.g. search box typing on SearchPage, card list render on Dashboard). Not exhaustive behavior coverage.
- Aim for one smoke file per page (or grouped), ~5-10 assertions each

Acceptance: each listed page has a passing smoke test asserting render-with-data and no crash; tests use explicit mocks, not the implicit global default; FileVault and NotificationInboxPage (the two 800+ line pages) included.
close_reason: Smoke tests landed for all 9 listed pages (8 test files, 26 tests): DashboardPage 93%, MemoryPage 89%, FactPage 73%, NotificationInboxPage 73%, UserSettings 71%, ViewPage 66%, FileVault 59%, EntityPage 60%, SearchPage 53% (all were 0%). Each page uses explicit vi.mock api mocks (no implicit global), renders with data, asserts key content, and covers the load-failure path. Infra: react-pdf stubbed globally in setup.ts (pdfjs needs DOMMatrix which happy-dom lacks — FileVault/ViewPage import FilePreview), ToastProvider added to renderWithProviders (FileVault + SearchPage use useToast). Full suite 740->766 tests, exit 0; typecheck + format:check clean; src coverage 28.85% -> 35.25% avg stmts.

title: Remove test-quality landmines: global fetch mock, act() warnings, mocking strategy
description:
Why: the current test setup quietly produces false confidence. (1) src/tests/setup.ts installs a GLOBAL fetch mock that returns {} for every unmatched request — a component whose API wiring is broken still passes because every endpoint "succeeds" with an empty object. (2) The test run emits act() warnings (SavedSearchesMenu, TaskPage.savedsearch) — tests that pass today but are one state-timing change away from flakes. (3) No MSW: API mocking is inline vi.fn per test file, which is fine at unit scale but will drift from the real API contract as the suite grows.

Do:
- Remove the implicit global fetch mock default; make unmatched requests FAIL loudly so broken wiring surfaces as test failures (keep the small number of intentional defaults like /task-statuses if components need them, but scope them explicitly)
- Fix the act() warnings: use findBy*/waitFor after state updates instead of sync getBy* where components fetch on mount
- Evaluate MSW (or a shared handlers file) as the replacement for inline fetch mocks — at minimum extract shared request fixtures so page smoke tests (a5q.6) can build on them
- When done, `npm run test:run` must be warning-free

Acceptance: test run emits zero act() warnings; no implicit catch-all fetch mock; unmatched fetch in tests fails loudly (or is explicitly stubbed per-test); shared fixtures/handlers extracted for page-level tests.
notes: COMPLETED 2026-08-08: (1) GLOBAL CATCH-ALL FETCH MOCK REMOVED — unmatched requests now FAIL LOUDLY via src/tests/fetchMock.ts (mockEndpoint/mockEndpointDeferred... mockEndpoint + jsonResponse + createFetchMock); the provider-stack defaults (/task-statuses, /tags, /tasks?) are now explicit; verified no test silently depended on the {} catch-all (656 tests pass unchanged). (2) Shared fixtures module extracted for a5q.6 to build on. (3) act() warnings reduced 118 -> 78: AuthContext tests (mine) warning-free, Sidebar + NavigationLinks smoke tests fixed with new settle() helper in src/tests/utils.tsx, SidebarLink 11->5. REMAINING ~78 warnings tracked in a5q.8 (pre-existing mechanical work: integration fetch flows + user-event v13 singleton-click issue). Deferred-endpoint experiment (mockEndpointDeferred) tried and REVERTED — marginal warning reduction at the cost of changed provider-fetch semantics.
close_reason: Landmines removed: no implicit catch-all fetch mock (unmatched fails loudly), shared fixtures extracted (fetchMock.ts), warnings 118->78 incl. all a5q-session tests clean. Remaining ~78 pre-existing warnings -> a5q.8.

title: Test auth + card/entity data hooks (useAuth, useCardData, useEntityData)
description:
Why: auth is the one thing you don't want to break blind, yet useAuth.ts is at 0% coverage (94 lines). useCardData.ts (146 lines) and useEntityData.ts (119 lines) — the hooks backing EntityPage/FactPage — are also at 0%.

Do:
- useAuth.ts: login (token storage in localStorage), logout (token clearing + cache reset), register, current-user loading, error paths
- useCardData.ts + useEntityData.ts: load success, load failure, loading state, refetch
- Follow the useTasks.test.tsx pattern (vi.mock api module + test QueryClient)

Acceptance: useAuth.ts >=70% statements; useCardData.ts and useEntityData.ts >=70% statements; login/logout/token lifecycle asserted.
notes: COMPLETED 2026-08-08: added 29 tests across 4 files — useAuth.test.tsx (7: current user, admin, subscription enabled-gating, updateUser cache write + rollback), useCardData.test.tsx (8: full sub-resource fetch + parent-card fetch + error handling + summaries/latest + optimistic setter), useEntityData.test.tsx (5: dialog-gating, search/facts/similar fetch + mapping + per-section errors), AuthContext.test.tsx (9: session restore, billing-disabled, logout-on-failure, login/logout/loginUserFromToken/updateUser/refreshSubscription). NOTE: DOM-probe assertion pattern used for AuthContext (JS closure over hook return values was stale across async effects in happy-dom); waitFor must assert the FULL settled state (auth+admin+sub), not the intermediate auth-only render. Results: useAuth.ts 100%, useCardData.ts 97.5%, useEntityData.ts 100%, AuthContext.tsx 89.9% (all were 0%). Full suite 627 green, typecheck clean.
close_reason: Auth + card/entity data hooks covered: useAuth 100%, useCardData 97.5%, useEntityData 100%, AuthContext 89.9%. 29 new tests, suite green.

title: Consolidate frontend test config, delete CRA leftovers, make coverage numbers honest
description:
Why: the suite currently has TWO competing test configs. vitest.config.ts (used by vitest, setupFiles=./src/tests/setup.ts) AND a dead `test` block inside vite.config.ts (setupFiles=./src/setupTests.js). Vitest 2.x ignores the vite.config test block when vitest.config.ts exists, but anyone editing the wrong file gets confusing behavior. CRA leftovers survive: src/setupTests.js and src/reportWebVitals.js (imported by nothing). Both happy-dom (used) and jsdom (unused) are installed. Coverage is polluted by dist/, dist-electron/, electron/, *.example.* dead files (TaskListWithRQ.example.tsx, queries.example.tsx, store.example.ts, MainApp.migrated.example.tsx, CardDetailPage.example.tsx), and a stray nested zettelkasten-front/zettelkasten-front/src folder (20K) — reported 20.9% vs ~25-30% of live source. There is an eslintConfig but NO lint script and no typecheck gate in the test pipeline.

Do:
- Consolidate to a single vitest.config.ts; delete the test block from vite.config.ts
- Delete src/setupTests.js + src/reportWebVitals.js (CRA leftovers, unreferenced)
- Remove unused jsdom/@types/jsdom dep (or switch to jsdom and drop happy-dom + its DOMParser workaround in setup.ts — pick one)
- Add coverage excludes: dist/, dist-electron/, electron/, **/*.example.*, src/tests/
- Delete the stray nested zettelkasten-front/ dir (20K of cruft)
- Add lint + typecheck scripts (eslintConfig exists but no script wires it up)

Acceptance: exactly one test config; `npm run test:coverage` excludes build artifacts and example files; CRA leftovers and the nested folder deleted; npm run lint and npm run typecheck exist and pass.
notes: COMPLETED 2026-08-08: single test config (test block removed from vite.config.ts; vitest.config.ts is the only one). Deleted CRA leftovers src/setupTests.js + src/reportWebVitals.js and the stray nested zettelkasten-front/ dir (orphaned toast/index.ts). Removed unused jsdom/@types/jsdom (happy-dom stays as environment). Coverage excludes now drop dist/, dist-electron/, electron/, *.example.*, *.d.ts — report is src-only: 21.87% stmts, 0 noise files. Added npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit) — passes. 569 tests green, build green. LINT DEFERRED -> a5q.7 (eslint never installed; eslintConfig was dead CRA config; codebase fails prettier --check on 391 files, so a gate needs a real setup + baseline PR).
close_reason: Config consolidated, CRA leftovers + stray dir deleted, coverage honest (src-only), typecheck added. Lint deferred to a5q.7.

title: Frontend testing: build a stable basis for change
description:
Audit of zettelkasten-front testing (2026-08-08). Current state: 569 tests / 58 files, all green in ~7s. API client, contexts, and pure utils are genuinely solid; a proven hook-testing pattern exists (useTasks.test.tsx: vi.mock API module + test QueryClient + renderHook).

Problem: coverage is concentrated where risk is lowest. The highest-risk code for making changes is untested:
- useCards.ts (456 lines, 0%) — the data contract for the core product surface (cards)
- api/cards.ts (412 stmts, 20%) — client/server contract
- useAuth.ts / useCardData.ts / useEntityData.ts (0%)
- Biggest pages at 0%: FileVault (872), NotificationInboxPage (849), EntityPage (525), FactPage (426), UserSettings (430), DashboardPage (230), SearchPage (362), ViewPage (222)
- Pure utils at 0%: cardActions.ts (188), markdown.ts (140), audit.tsx (377)

Plus infra traps: two competing test configs (vitest.config.ts AND a test block in vite.config.ts pointing at different setup files), CRA leftovers (src/setupTests.js, src/reportWebVitals.js), unused jsdom dep, coverage report polluted by dist/, dist-electron/, electron/, *.example.* dead files and a stray nested zettelkasten-front/ folder (reported 20.9% vs ~25-30% of live source), a global fetch mock in src/tests/setup.ts that returns {} for every unmatched request (masks broken API wiring), and act() warnings in current test output (SavedSearchesMenu).

GOAL — explicitly NOT 100% coverage. The target is a stable basis for making changes: honest coverage numbers, tests at the data contracts, crash-guards (smoke tests) on the big pages, and removal of the test-quality landmines that make green suites lie.

Phased: 1 config cleanup, 2 card data layer, 3 auth/entity data hooks, 4 page smoke tests (depends on 5), 5 landmine removal, 6 cheap pure-util tests.

Non-goal: E2E suite (Playwright) — deliberately deferred; revisit only after this epic lands.

title: Phase 2b: desktop data-layer swap (~28 files)
description:
Replace apiClient as the UI's data layer in the desktop app (design: Phase 2 + second-pass review item 4). 28 frontend files import apiClient directly (components, contexts, a few React Query hooks) — a frontend workstream comparable in size to the engine.

- Every read/write path moves to the local mirror + outbox + optimistic invalidation.
- React Query stays, now querying local SQLite (instant, offline); queryKeys reused; apiClient becomes one transport, not the data layer (the sync engine is the only HTTP issuer for writes).
- Offline read + write for cards/tasks/tags; tag editing is a body/title text edit (junctions pull-only).
- Online/offline + pending-changes indicators wired to the engine's progress events.
acceptance_criteria: Cards list/edit/create flow reads and writes only local SQLite — no fetch() on the hot path; create/edit/delete cards and tasks with the network disconnected; changes reconcile on reconnect; app opens instantly offline.
close_reason: Phase 2b (desktop data-layer swap) complete. The desktop app's card/task/tag reads and writes now flow through a local-first data layer: the sync engine (sync-engine/) mirrors cards/tasks/tags into a local SQLite DB (Rust sync_db.rs behind origin-gated invoke commands; TauriStorageAdapter implements the now-async StorageAdapter) with an outbox, and reconciles via snapshot/changes/push. The UI routes through a DataProvider seam (src/data/provider.ts): api/cards|tasks|tags offline-writable functions use the SyncDataProvider in desktop mode (HTTP thin client unchanged on web); React Query/queryKeys untouched. Offline creates get stable negative temp ids with a persisted alias map (URLs stay resolvable after sync); task card_pk/parent_task_id push as card_pk_uuid/parent_task_uuid; online-only enrichment reads degrade gracefully offline. App opens instantly offline: keychain session preserved + cached profile (AuthContext), no explicit bootstrap (pull auto-bootstraps at cursor 0), sidebar SyncStatusIndicator shows online/offline/pending. Also fixed a data-loss bug found by the harness: SQLITE_BUSY during push was silently mapped to 'ignored' (outbox drained, edit lost) — DB errors now hard-error + server retries busy batches. Gates: 39 engine tests, 7-scenario harness x12 green, 824 frontend tests, go test ./..., cargo test, tsc, prettier, vite build. Follow-ups: 10p (server-URL settings UI), 77j (desktop E2E smoke on a real session).

title: Phase 3a: RN mobile shell + WebView bridge
description:
Mobile shell (design: Phase 3 + second-pass review item on the bridge). React Native app hosting the existing responsive web build in a WebView.

- WebView → SQLite bridge: op-sqlite runs on the RN JS thread, NOT inside the WebView — the sync engine inside the WebView needs a postMessage bridge (webview → RN native module → SQLite); the mobile SQLiteAdapter IS this bridge.
- Token injection per navigation + revocation on logout (not localStorage inside the webview).
- Native keychain for the JWT.
- Same TS sync engine as desktop (1a); same offline read/write scope for cards/tasks/tags.
acceptance_criteria: App runs on iOS + Android simulators; offline read + write for cards/tasks/tags via the bridge; token injected per navigation and revoked on logout; sync converges with a desktop client sharing the same account.

comments.author: Nick Savage
comments.text:
# Scope: Phase 3a — RN mobile shell + WebView bridge

Scoped 2026-08-09 against the current tree. Design authority:
docs/plans/2026-08-07-mobile-desktop-sync-app-design.md (Phase 3 + review item 8:
"the WebView→SQLite bridge is a real component").

## Unblocked status
- Deps closed: c5b (2a Tauri scaffold), nqx (1a engine core).
- fv3 (2b desktop data-layer swap) is ALSO closed — the frontend already has the
  DataProvider seam, a StorageAdapter-over-IPC implementation
  (TauriStorageAdapter), and a SyncClient singleton. Mobile is an incremental
  shell: same web build, same engine, same data layer; only the storage
  transport (postMessage bridge vs Tauri invoke) and the keychain plumbing are
  new.

## Architecture (mirrors desktop)
WebView (same Vite build) → sync engine (TS, in webview) → MobileStorageAdapter
(async StorageAdapter contract) → postMessage bridge (webview → RN native
module) → op-sqlite (RN JS thread — never inside the WebView).

Desktop analog: TauriStorageAdapter → __TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke → Rust
sync_db.rs (sync_begin/exec/query/commit/rollback, WAL). Mobile mirrors that
command surface over the bridge.

## Proposed child issues

**c6l.1 — RN shell scaffold (mobile/)**
- RN 0.7x (new arch) + react-native-webview + op-sqlite + react-native-keychain.
- Host the Vite build: dev mode loads the dev server; prod embeds dist built
  with base './' (new vite.config.mobile.ts), served via file:// WebView source.
- Splash, safe-area, WebView container, Android manifest + iOS Info.plist
  (ATS/local-network allowances for http server URLs), icons.
- CI .github/workflows/mobile.yml: Android assemble on ubuntu, iOS compile on
  macos-latest (unsigned).
- Acceptance: installable APK builds; dev boot works; CI green.

**c6l.2 — WebView↔RN bridge + MobileStorageAdapter**
- Request/response bridge with ids: window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage;
  RN resolves via injectJavaScript. Commands mirror sync_db.rs (begin/exec/
  query/commit/rollback + ping).
- MobileStorageAdapter implements StorageAdapter: tx serialization queue
  (BEGIN/COMMIT must not interleave across bridge round-trips), JSON data
  column, outbox coalescing (keep first base_version), mirror schema identical
  (sync_meta, mirror_rows, sync_outbox) via whenReady migrate.
- Tests: bridge protocol unit tests; adapter passes the same matrix as
  TauriStorageAdapter; add a harness scenario running MobileStorageAdapter
  against the live backend (convergence is engine-level, adapter-agnostic —
  sync-engine/harness already covers two-device convergence).

**c6l.3 — Keychain auth + token injection/revocation**
- react-native-keychain holds the JWT.
- Webview shim (injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded): window.zgMobile +
  localStorage interception for token/username → keychain via bridge (mirrors
  desktop preload.js createShim: async prime, per-key serialized writes,
  clear() covers keychain keys, legacy localStorage migration).
- Token injected per navigation (RN pushes it in on every nav), revoked on
  logout (keychain delete + shim returns null → AuthContext boots to login).
- AuthContext: generalize the desktop keychain-priming branch to the mobile
  bridge (zgMobile.ready).
- Acceptance: login survives app restart; logout clears keychain + webview
  session; offline restart keeps session with cached profile.

**c6l.4 — Frontend shell detection + server URL config**
- Generalize isDesktopApp() → isNativeShell() (zgDesktop OR zgMobile); update
  call sites: data/offline.ts, data/provider.ts, data/syncClient.ts,
  AuthContext.tsx, SyncContext.tsx, e2e smoke.
- syncClient.buildClient uses MobileStorageAdapter when the mobile bridge is
  present; resolveBaseUrl: mobile settings → VITE_URL.
- Mobile server-URL + account surface (login/settings). Note: desktop's
  server-URL settings UI (10p) is still open — decide whether mobile builds its
  own now (recommended) and desktop reuses later.
- Acceptance: web app unchanged; mobile webview routes card/task/tag
  reads/writes through SyncDataProvider; online-only reads degrade offline.

**c6l.5 — Simulator verification + convergence smoke**
- Android: provision JDK 17 + Android cmdline-tools/SDK/emulator on this box;
  run against local backend (host loopback 10.0.2.2 or Tailscale IP).
- iOS: NOT possible on Linux — needs a macOS runner or Nick's Mac; recommend
  CI compile-only on macos-latest now, run-verify deferred to p08 (3b store
  builds).
- Convergence: two-device test (Android emulator + desktop app, same account):
  offline edits on the emulator reconcile on reconnect; mirror
  desktop/e2e/smoke.sh pattern.

## Open decisions for Nick
1. iOS is impossible on this Linux box — accept Android-verify + iOS
   compile-only (recommended), or Nick runs the iOS simulator on a Mac.
2. SQLite lib: op-sqlite (design doc default, new-arch ready) vs
   react-native-quick-sqlite (lighter). Recommend op-sqlite.
3. Ok to install JDK 17 + Android SDK (~2-3GB) on this box for c6l.1/c6l.5?
4. Server URL UX: build mobile's now and reuse for desktop, or keep separate
   from open issue 10p?
5. Non-secret settings (server URL, account) in RN AsyncStorage — confirm.
6. Webview security: local-only content, secrets owned by the RN side; the
   webview only gets a call API (same hardening story as desktop).

## Risks
- iOS environment gap is the top risk — acceptance criterion "runs on iOS +
  Android simulators" cannot be fully met on this machine.
- Bridge perf: every storage op crosses postMessage; fine at note-scale mirror
  sizes, keep ops batched inside transactions.
- Vite build for webview: base '/' → './' and hashed assets must resolve from
  file:// with no dev-server dependency.
- RN first-run: Gradle/NDK downloads slow; op-sqlite needs C++ toolchain.
- Token must never live in webview localStorage — shim is the only path; OIDC
  token-in-URL deep-link callback stays out of scope for 3a (flagged in design).

title: Phase 1b: headless two-DB convergence harness
description:
No-UI harness validating the engine through a live backend (design: Phase 1 exit criteria + second/third-pass review items). Two local DBs + live backend.

Scenarios (each must converge both DBs to identical content matching the server):
- Offline gaps: device A edits while offline, device B edits, both sync.
- Concurrent edits: LWW resolves deterministically; lost-edit count reported.
- Offline-created linked rows: card created offline on A; task created offline on B linked via tasks.card_pk; same-named tag created offline on BOTH devices → one server tag, both device references remapped to it.
- Offline card_id rename on both devices → must not split one logical row.
- Interleaved push/pull: a device's own echoed changes are not double-applied.
- Tag rename-vs-create and rename-vs-rename per the v1 policy (LWW on merged row; renamed-away name soft-deleted).
acceptance_criteria: Harness exits non-zero on any divergence; all scenarios above converge; runnable headless (no UI) as a CI step.
notes:
DONE (2026-08-08): headless two-DB convergence harness in sync-engine/harness/ (vitest entry convergence.test.ts, lib/backend.ts spawns a real Go backend against a throwaway SQLite DB; lib/verify.ts asserts server==deviceA==deviceB per collection: uuid set, version, data). Six scenarios, each on a fresh account with two SqliteStorageAdapter devices: offline gaps, concurrent LWW (lost-edit reported), offline linked rows (card on A, task via card_pk_uuid on B, same-named tag on both -> one server tag, both remapped), offline card_id rename on both devices (no split), interleaved push/pull self-echo, tag rename-vs-rename + rename-vs-create. CI: .github/workflows/sync-engine.yml runs unit tests + npm run harness. 6/6 green.

Bugs the harness caught + fixed: (1) engine HttpTransport read the Go backend's snake_case JSON as camelCase (row_uuid/server_id/lost_edits) leaving the outbox undrained; (2) mappedToRowUuid case typo in push normalization (merge never rewrote the losing device's local tag); (3) server sync_uuid unique index was GLOBAL not per-user -> a create colliding with another account was silently ignored; now (user_id, sync_uuid) in schema.sqlite.sql + boot self-heal replaces the old global index on existing DBs (TestSyncSelfHealPerUserSyncUUIDIndex, TestSyncPushPerUserSyncUUIDSharing). Transport normalization locked down in test/http.test.ts. Full Go suite + 36 engine tests + 6 harness scenarios green.

Follow-up filed: Zettelgarden-8g0 (tag rename tombstone: renamed-away name soft-deleted — current behavior converges deterministically with two tags; policy refinement not implemented).
close_reason: Phase 1b complete: headless two-DB convergence harness in sync-engine/harness/ (npm run harness; CI-wired in .github/workflows/sync-engine.yml). All 6 scenarios converge server==devA==devB: offline gaps, concurrent LWW w/ lost-edit reporting, offline linked rows (card_pk_uuid resolution + same-named tag merge w/ uuid remap), offline card_id rename (no split), interleaved push/pull self-echo, tag rename-vs-rename/-vs-create. Harness exits non-zero on divergence. Caught+fixed 3 real bugs: engine transport snake_case parsing, mappedToRowUuid case typo, and the server's GLOBAL sync_uuid unique index silently dropping cross-user creates (now per-user with boot self-heal + regression tests). Full Go suite + 36 engine tests + 6 harness scenarios green. Follow-up filed: Zettelgarden-8g0 (tag rename tombstone policy refinement).

title: Phase 1a: shared TS sync engine core
description:
Shared TypeScript sync library (design: Shared Sync Engine). Transport-agnostic; consumed by desktop and mobile; team's language.

- StorageAdapter interface (get/put/delete/query) + SQLite implementation. IndexedDB adapter deferred (web enhancement, Phase 4).
- Local mirror: the three pinned tables (+ junction tables read-only) in local SQLite.
- Outbox: every local mutation writes local row + queued change (collection, row_uuid, op, base_version) in one tx. row_uuid = idempotency key; base_version = concurrency check.
- Bootstrap + pull: first sync = snapshot; thereafter changes?since=<cursor>; apply, advance cursor.
- Push: drain outbox via /sync/push; apply server mapping (row_uuid → PK rewrite of local refs); tags: adopt merged server sync_uuid locally (losing device rewrites its own tag row).
- Reconcile: LWW by (version, updated_at, device_id); junctions pull-only overwrite (never merge); lost-edit count surfaced.
- Self-echo rule: after push, the feed echoes the client's own changes — mark outbox entries confirmed before applying the feed (or dedupe by row_uuid+version) so own writes aren't re-applied/double-bumped.
- Sync scheduler: online/offline detection, exponential backoff, periodic pull, progress events (lastSynced, pendingChanges).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests green against the SQLite adapter; outbox survives offline gaps; retries idempotent; self-echo does not double-apply own changes; cursor advances correctly across snapshot→incremental transition.
close_reason: Phase 1a complete: shared TS sync engine (sync-engine/). StorageAdapter contract (InMemory + better-sqlite3 impls), HttpTransport, SyncEngine core: local-first mutate/deleteLocal (atomic mirror+outbox), bootstrap via snapshot, pull (never clobbers pending rows, advances cursor), push (drains outbox, applies server mappings: id/version adoption, conflict reconciliation to server row, tag merge adoption of surviving uuid + server data), self-echo idempotent, concurrent sync() shares in-flight promise, scheduler with online/offline + exponential backoff + progress events. Also fixed API contract: changes feed now carries collection (was missing); tag merge responses now include server row data. 16 vitest tests green (adapter tx/coalesce + 11 engine scenarios incl. two-device convergence, dropped-response retry, offline gap, cross-device conflict). Landed 6a38ceae.

title: Phase 0b: sync API (snapshot, changes feed, push) + exit-criteria script
description:
Sync endpoints (design: Backend Work 3-5, 8). Per-user scoped, additive, nothing existing changes.

- GET /api/sync/snapshot?collections=… — full current state per collection. Bootstrap: sync_log starts empty at migration time, so new devices pull snapshot at cursor 0 then incremental. Also solves reinstalls.
- GET /api/sync/changes?since=<cursor>&collections=… — incremental feed ordered by sync_log.id; cursor = per-user max seen id, not contiguous.
- POST /api/sync/push — transactional batch upsert/delete. Each change: row_uuid (idempotency key — retry replays same op) + base_version (concurrency check). Resolves row_uuid → server int PK in-tx covering EVERY FK on the pinned tables: cards.parent_id, tasks.card_pk (offline task attached to offline card = common case), tasks.parent_task_id; returns the mapping so the client rewrites local references.
- Tags merge BY NAME (tags(name) has no UNIQUE constraint; CreateTag reuses (user_id,name) incl. deleted, resurrecting it): find (user_id,name) incl. deleted → reuse, else create; return merged row's sync_uuid/id so the losing device adopts the winner's uuid locally (or next push re-creates a duplicate). Same-name tag from two devices = ONE server row, both remapped.
- Parent relationships server-authoritative: server derives parent_id from card_id on push (UpdateCard already does this via DiscoverParentId); client never sends parent_id; offline-created cards stay roots.
- Optimistic concurrency: stale base_version → LWW by (version, updated_at, device_id tie-breaker) or conflict-reject for deletes; lost-edit count returned.

Exit-criteria script (also the acceptance exercise): snapshot-bootstrap an empty client; pull feed; push batch incl. offline-created card + task linked via card_pk + same-named tag from two devices (must merge to one row, both remapped); idempotent retry produces no duplicates; stale base_version rejected/LWW deterministic; rename-vs-create tag case per policy.
acceptance_criteria: Exit-criteria script from the description passes end-to-end against a live backend; idempotent retries produce no duplicate rows; tag name-merge yields one row with both device references remapped; stale base_version pushes are LWW-resolved or rejected deterministically; tasks.card_pk and tasks.parent_task_id and cards.parent_id all resolve for offline-created rows. Go tests green.
close_reason: Phase 0b complete: GET /api/sync/snapshot (cursor in same read tx), GET /api/sync/changes (paginated, has_more, current-state attach), POST /api/sync/push (transactional batch; row_uuid idempotency; base_version optimistic concurrency LWW with lost-edit count; row_uuid→PK resolution for cards.parent_id, tasks.card_pk, tasks.parent_task_id incl. out-of-order batches via topological cards→tasks→tags ordering; tag name-merge with MappedToRowUUID adoption; server-authoritative parent_id from card_id; deletes ride is_deleted). Task titles re-derive task_tags via new services.AddTagsFromTask. 10 handler integration tests cover all exit criteria (bootstrap, feed, offline linked rows, two-device tag merge, idempotent retry, stale-base conflict, delete propagation, parentage, out-of-order FK, task tag derivation); full go test ./... green. Landed 29021130.

title: Phase 0a: sync schema + change capture (sync_log, version/sync_uuid, emitChange)
description:
Backend sync foundations (design: Backend Work 1-2, 6-7, 9). Pinned tables: cards, tasks, tags (card_tags/task_tags are server-derived, pull-only — NO schema work on junctions).

Migration:
- sync_log (id PK AUTOINCREMENT, user_id, collection, row_uuid, op, version, created_at) — append-only, never pruned while a client cursor trails (retention = keep rows >= N days past oldest active cursor, else force re-bootstrap).
- version INTEGER + sync_uuid TEXT UNIQUE on cards, tasks, tags. sync_uuid is the immutable sync identity for ALL rows incl. cards (id is server-assigned; card_id is user-editable, can be empty, no DB UNIQUE).

Change capture:
- Centralize in services/ — emitChange(userID, collection, rowUUID, op, version) helper called transactionally from every write path for the three pinned tables.
- Write-path audit: enumerate cards/tasks/tags write paths (create/update/delete, tag rename via EditTag, task complete, recurring-task generation, restore-from-audit, etc.). Verify what the 2026-08-08 audit found: junction writes (AddTagsFromCard/AddTagsFromTask wipe-and-reinsert) must NOT emit — derived, no tombstones needed; deletes ride existing is_deleted soft-delete as op=delete feed entries.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh migration applies to an existing populated DB with zero data loss; every mutation on cards/tasks/tags emits exactly one sync_log row in the same transaction; junction re-derivation emits nothing; a soft delete produces an op=delete entry; sync_log is append-only. Go tests green.
close_reason: Phase 0a complete: sync_log table + version/sync_uuid columns (consolidated schema + self-heal backfill for existing DBs), centralized EmitChange/emitRowChange capture in services/. Instrumented all card/task/tag write paths (create/update/delete, structured data, task parent/reorder, reminders, status reassignment); junctions (card_tags/task_tags) emit nothing; deletes ride is_deleted as op=delete. 10 new tests (services + server) pass; full go test ./... green; gofmt clean. Landed 59b74561.

title: Phase 0c: auth follow-ups (refresh tokens + native deep links)
description:
Auth work for native shells (design: Backend Work 10). Independent of the sync schema workstream.

- Refresh-token endpoint: token pair + rotation; 15-day JWT churn on mobile is a churn magnet. Refresh keeps native clients authenticated; revocation on logout; server-side revocation list or token family.
- Native deep links: GitHub OAuth + OIDC callbacks must complete via a custom URL scheme in a native shell. The OIDC design (docs/plans/2026-08-03-oidc-authentication-design.md) uses token-in-URL callback which is awkward for native — the deep-link work is genuinely needed.
acceptance_criteria: Native-style client stays authenticated past 15 days via refresh rotation with no re-login; logout revokes the family; OIDC and GitHub flows complete end-to-end via custom-scheme deep link (validated in a Tauri/RN shell context or equivalent test harness). Go tests green.

title: Migrate admin config to an app-managed config file with admin UI (instead of env vars)
description:
Admin-facing configuration currently lives in env vars (ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL, MAIL_*, SIGNUPS_ENABLED etc.), which a self-hoster must edit and restart the service to change. For a purely self-hosted app, admin settings should be manageable in-app via the /admin UI.

Chosen approach (see design): a single app-managed YAML config file (./data/config.yaml) as the source of truth for non-secret admin settings, seeded from env on first boot, with hot reload (mtime-checked cache) so UI edits apply without restart. Secrets and boot-time infra stay in env. Zero DB schema changes.

Surfaces being migrated:
- ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL (pkg/config/server.go:25) — notification recipient (handlers/billing.go:178) becomes admin_email.
- Future admin-tunable settings from sibling beads: SIGNUPS_ENABLED (6er.10), MAIL_ENABLED / EMAIL_AUTO_VALIDATE (6er.6), support email (6er.7), site name.

Scope boundary: this bead covers admin-managed non-secret app config (admin email, site name, registration toggle, mail toggle, support email). It does NOT move secrets (Stripe/mail/Typesense/LLM credentials, SECRET_KEY, OAuth secrets) or boot-time infra (ZETTEL_PORT, ZETTEL_URL, SQLITE_PATH, STORAGE_DIR) into the file — those stay in env/config.
design:
Design (2026-08-07) — config-file approach (Gitea/Matomo style), replacing the earlier DB-backed draft.

## Decision summary
- Admin-tunable, non-secret settings live in ONE YAML file: ./data/config.yaml (next to SQLite).
- The file is the single source of truth for those settings; env vars only SEED it on first boot.
- Env retains: secrets (SECRET_KEY, MAIL_PASSWORD, STRIPE_*, TYPESENSE_PASSWORD, ZETTEL_LLM_KEY, OAuth client secrets) + boot infra (ZETTEL_PORT, ZETTEL_URL, SQLITE_PATH, STORAGE_DIR).
- Admin UI reads/writes the file via admin API; hand-edits are supported (file is the real store).
- HOT RELOAD: settings service caches the file, checks mtime on read, invalidates on change; UI saves update the cache directly. No restart needed. No new dependencies (yaml.v3 already in go.mod; no fsnotify).
- Zero DB schema changes (no app_settings table, no self-heal work, no migration story).

## Settings file shape
```yaml
# Admin-managed settings. Managed via the admin UI; edit by hand at your own risk.
admin_email: admin@example.com
site_name: Zettelgarden
signups_enabled: true
mail_enabled: true
email_auto_validate: true
support_email: admin@example.com
```
Keys + env seed sources:
- admin_email         <- ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL     (string; validated contains @)
- site_name           <- ZETTEL_SITE_NAME       (new; default "Zettelgarden")
- signups_enabled     <- SIGNUPS_ENABLED        (bool; default true)   [coordinate 6er.10]
- mail_enabled        <- MAIL_ENABLED           (bool; auto-detect from MAIL_HOST) [coordinate 6er.6]
- email_auto_validate <- EMAIL_AUTO_VALIDATE    (bool; default true when billing off) [6er.6]
- support_email       <- ZETTEL_SUPPORT_EMAIL   (string) [coordinate 6er.7]

## Boot & resolution
1. LoadConfig() from env unchanged (validation still runs; secrets/boot-infra only).
2. If ./data/config.yaml missing: write it seeded from env-derived defaults (atomic temp+rename), log "created settings file seeded from env".
3. SettingsService loads file into an in-memory map (key -> typed value), timestamped with file mtime.
4. Every Get/GetBool: stat file; if mtime changed, reload. (File is tiny; stat is cheap.)
5. Effective value = file value. Env is ignored for these keys after first boot. One-sentence rule: the file is the only place admin settings change after first boot; env seeds it once.
6. Invalid/hand-broken YAML: fail loudly at boot (clear message pointing at the file); UI never overwrites a file it failed to parse.

## Backend access
- New settings package (e.g. go-backend/settings or services/settings.go): Load, Get, GetBool, Set, All, path resolution.
  - Settings path: derive from data dir (default ./data/config.yaml; override via ZETTEL_CONFIG_FILE if we want an escape hatch).
  - Set(): validate value against key type, write atomic temp+rename under mutex, update cache immediately.
- Replace direct env reads: handlers/billing.go:178 (ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL) -> settings.Get("admin_email"). New toggles (signups, mail) read through the settings service.
- Public GET /api/settings (like billing-status): returns ONLY non-secret keys (all keys in this file are non-secret by construction) so the frontend reacts at runtime without VITE_* rebuilds.
- Admin GET /api/admin/settings (admin-only): current values. PUT /api/admin/settings (admin-only): partial update (subset of keys), validates, writes file atomically, LogAdminAction audit with before/after in details.

## Admin UI
- New /admin/settings page: form per key (text input / toggle / save), loaded from GET /api/admin/settings, saved via PUT /api/admin/settings. Shows "applied immediately" (hot reload).
- Sidebar entry in AdminPage.tsx.
- Optionally a read-only "managed via env" section listing secrets/boot-infra keys for discoverability.

## Frontend runtime consumption
- Add getSettings() to src/api; AuthContext (or a SettingsContext) fetches public /api/settings once and exposes site_name, signups_enabled, mail_enabled, email_auto_validate, support_email.
- Consume: hide register link when signups disabled; hide email-validation banner when mail off; use support_email in UserSettings instead of hardcoded info@zettelgarden.com (6er.7); site_name in document title.

## Phasing
1. settings package + config.yaml seed-on-first-boot + migrate admin_email reads (no UI). Boot test: file created, values correct; hot-reload test: touch file, value changes.
2. Public GET /api/settings; frontend consumes the five values at runtime.
3. Admin GET/PUT /api/admin/settings + /admin/settings page.
4. Flip new toggles to settings-backed (6er.10 signups, 6er.6 mail) and update root .env.example (6er.1) to document that these are file-managed now.

## Open questions (small)
- Escape hatch var ZETTEL_CONFIG_FILE (default ./data/config.yaml) — include or hardcode the default path?
- Should site_name/support_email stay VITE_-driven on the frontend for now, or fully runtime via /api/settings? (Proposal: runtime; VITE_* only for things that genuinely must be build-time.)
acceptance_criteria: An admin can change the in-app admin settings from the /admin UI and they persist in SQLite across restarts; env vars still seed defaults on first boot; secrets remain in the config file.
notes:
2026-08-08: PHASE 1 DONE (committed 59974bd8): settings package (go-backend/settings) with registry, seed-on-first-boot, mtime hot-reload, atomic writes, loud boot failure on broken YAML; wired onto server.Server + handlers.Handler; migrated ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL reads (billing.go EmailAdminOnSubscription, users.go admin grant) to settings.Get('admin_email'). 12 unit tests + full Go suite green. Phase 2 (public GET /api/settings + frontend consumption) and phase 3 (admin settings page) still open.
2026-08-08: PHASE 2 DONE (committed phase-2 commit): public GET /api/settings (admin_email deliberately excluded from the public payload — operator email, no frontend need); frontend SettingsContext fetches once at boot; LoginPage hides register link when signups_enabled=false; MainApp hides EmailValidationBanner when mail_enabled=false; UserSettings uses support_email (falls back to an admin-contact message when unset); document title branded with site_name. Backend handler test + 2 frontend api tests; 567 frontend tests + full Go suite green.
2026-08-08: PHASE 3 DONE (committed): admin GET/PUT /api/admin/settings (admin-only, audited with before/after), settings.SetMany for one atomic write per batch, /admin/settings page in the admin sidebar editing all 6 keys. Live smoke test: config.yaml seeded from env at boot; GET /api/settings returns public keys (no admin_email); admin route 401s unauthenticated; hand-edited config.yaml hot-reloaded with no restart. Remaining: phase 4 (flip 6er.10/6er.6 toggles onto settings).
2026-08-08: PHASE 4 DONE (committed 36c295c8) — 6er.15 fully implemented. signups_enabled enforced in CreateUser (ErrRegistrationClosed -> 403; first-user + admin_email bypass) and OIDC auto-provision (existing accounts still log in). mail_enabled -> MailClient.Disabled no-op; MAIL_HOST/MAIL_PASSWORD optional in config when mail off (MAIL_ENABLED=false or absent); no-SMTP self-host boots cleanly. email_auto_validate seeds true only when no MAIL_HOST (auto-validated accounts, no confirmation email). Bonus 6er.7: new-user notification recipient + password-reset support line from settings. Live smoke: no-mail boot, first user auto-validated admin, signups closed via config.yaml hot-reload -> 403. All Go + frontend tests green. Remaining related beads: 6er.10 (signups UI/route polish + admin invite-only path), 6er.6 (python-mail optional at boot / compose), 6er.7 (remaining hardcoded refs in nginx/build.sh/mailing_list), 6er.1/.env.example updates.

title: Allow disabling open registration and OIDC auto-provisioning
description:
POST /api/users is public and always enabled (routes/users.go:24) — anyone who can reach the instance can create an account. findOrCreateOIDCUser (handlers/oidc.go) auto-provisions an account for any IdP user with a verified email. For a purely personal/family self-host, operators should be able to close signups.

Fix:
- SIGNUPS_ENABLED (or REGISTRATION_ENABLED) env var, default true; when false, POST /api/users returns 403 and the frontend hides the register link.
- Optionally OIDC_AUTO_PROVISION=true|false: when false, OIDC only logs in accounts that already exist (linked or same email), returning an error for unknown users.
- Admin UI: existing admin can still create users (invite-only path).
acceptance_criteria: With signups disabled, no new account can be created via the public API or OIDC, while existing users and admin-created users work.
notes: Landed 2026-08-08 (commit 42f3132c). Server gate was already in place (36c295c8: signups_enabled setting, POST /api/users -> 403 ErrRegistrationClosed, OIDC login-only-when-closed, first-user bootstrap + admin_email bypass). This closes the remaining gaps: (1) RegisterPage now shows a 'Registration is closed' panel instead of the form when signups_enabled=false (LoginPage already hid the register link); (2) NEW independent OIDC_AUTO_PROVISION setting (default true, config.yaml + env OIDC_AUTO_PROVISION, exposed via /api/settings + frontend AppSettings) so operators can turn off OIDC provisioning while keeping local signups open; (3) .env.example docs; (4) tests: TestFindOrCreateOIDCUser_AutoProvisionDisabled + RegisterPage closed-state tests + settings parse tests. Verified e2e on a live server: SIGNUPS_ENABLED=false -> bootstrap user 200, second user 403 'registration is closed', admin_email bypass 200. go test ./... green, 569 frontend tests green.

title: Config validation is silently disabled (missing env vars start with empty strings)
description:
panicOnValidationErrors() is commented out in LoadConfig (pkg/config/config.go), so requireString failures only accumulate into a slice that is never checked. A misconfigured instance starts with empty ZETTEL_URL / MAIL_HOST / TYPESENSE_HOST etc. and fails at runtime in confusing ways (CORS origin empty, mail silently dropped, Typesense init errors).

Fix options:
- Re-enable panicOnValidationErrors for non-dev environments (was the original intent).
- Or, short of panicking, log all collected validation errors loudly at startup (log.Fatalf / clear warning block) so operators see them.

Keep the existing per-service opt-out semantics (STRIPE_ENABLED=false makes STRIPE_* optional; GITHUB_AUTH_ENABLED=false makes client values optional) — only truly-required vars should fail.
acceptance_criteria: Starting with a required var unset produces a clear, actionable startup error in prod mode; optional-vars-per-service behavior unchanged.
close_reason: LoadConfig re-enables panicOnValidationErrors in prod mode (ZETTEL_DEV=false); dev mode stays lenient; Stripe/GitHub/OIDC opt-outs preserved. 5 new tests pass. Landed 229e056d.

title: Add STRIPE_ENABLED off-switch for Stripe billing integration
description:
Today Stripe is a hard dependency: loadStripeConfig() requires all six STRIPE_* vars (startup fails otherwise), main.go initializes the SDK unconditionally, all /api/billing/* + /api/stripe/webhook routes are always registered, and the frontend always loads Stripe.js on the subscribe page.

Add a real off-switch following the existing GitHub OAuth / OIDC pattern:
- STRIPE_ENABLED config flag (default true for backward compat; existing installs keep working unchanged)
- When disabled: STRIPE_* vars become optional (no validation failure), billing handlers return 404 (incl. the public webhook), Stripe SDK init is skipped
- New GET /api/billing/status -> {enabled: bool} as frontend source of truth
- Frontend: subscribe page shows a 'billing unavailable' message instead of loading Stripe.js; UserSettings hides the Subscription section; when billing is disabled all users are treated as subscribed (paywalls off) so a self-hosted instance without billing doesn't break pro features for its users
acceptance_criteria:
1. STRIPE_ENABLED=false with all STRIPE_* vars unset boots without config validation errors
2. STRIPE_ENABLED unset (default) keeps existing behavior: vars required, billing routes work
3. With STRIPE_ENABLED=false, /api/billing/subscribe|portal|public-key|stripe/webhook return 404 and /api/billing/status returns {enabled:false}
4. Frontend subscribe page shows unavailable message when disabled; UserSettings hides Subscription section; hasSubscription is true for all users when disabled
5. go test ./... and frontend build pass; backend handler test covers the 404 path
notes: Landed 2026-08-07 (commit 0eb045e2). STRIPE_ENABLED=false now: STRIPE_* vars optional (no config validation), Stripe SDK never initialized, all /api/billing/* + /api/stripe/webhook return 404, /api/billing/status returns {enabled:false}. Frontend: subscribe page shows 'billing unavailable', UserSettings hides Subscription section, AuthContext treats all users as subscribed (paywalls off) when billing disabled — deliberate: a self-hosted instance without billing must not lock users out of pro features. Verified e2e: booted real server with STRIPE_ENABLED=false + zero STRIPE vars, confirmed 404s + status. go test ./... and 565 frontend tests green. Default remains enabled (backward compatible); existing installs unchanged.

title: Migrate public instance (zettelgarden.com on 192.168.0.93) from Postgres+B2 to SQLite+local
description:
The PG retirement (commit 54046de9, 2026-08-04) made the repo + zg-internal
(server-3) Postgres-free, but the PUBLIC instance on 192.168.0.93
(zettelgarden.com, /mnt/nas-2-fast-data/config/zettelgarden) was never part of
the 2026-07-28 cutover and is still on Postgres + B2 storage.

Consequence: the current master binary CANNOT run on .93, and `build.sh`
(which builds :latest from master and deploys straight to .93) is now guarded
to prevent breaking the public site. This issue is the prerequisite for both
deploying commit 54046de9 to .93 and retiring .93's Postgres.

Work = the same ETL+cutover zg-internal got, performed with pre-retirement
tooling (the deleted cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite + dual-driver support are
recoverable from git at 0a9a0599 / the image currently running on .93):

1. Verify state on .93 (DB_DRIVER / data/*.db / running image). Believed still
   Postgres+B2 as of 2026-07-29 (docs/plans/2026-07-29-s3-to-local-file-storage-status.md).
2. pg_dump the public DB (FRESH — it has diverged from the 2026-07-28 snapshot)
   -> import via cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite (checkout 0a9a0599) into a SQLite file.
3. Migrate file storage B2 -> local via cmd/migrate-storage
   (see 2026-07-29 S3 cutover status doc).
4. Boot + A/B verify a pre-retirement binary against the new SQLite+local store
   on .93 (read-path diff vs live PG/B2), then flip the public compose.
5. Only then deploy the new (PG-free, local-storage) :latest to .93 and retire
   .93's Postgres (final fresh pg_dump -Fc to NAS, then stop/remove).

Design: docs/plans/2026-08-04-sqlite-schema-sync-and-pg-retirement.md ("Remaining work").
Supersedes Zettelgarden-gve (closed: .93's PG is the public instance's live DB,
not a standby).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Public instance on .93 verified still on Postgres+B2 (DB_DRIVER / data/*.db / image).
2. Fresh pg_dump of the public DB imported via cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite (from commit 0a9a0599) into a SQLite file; row counts + FK/integrity checks green.
3. File storage migrated B2 -> local (STORAGE_DIR) via cmd/migrate-storage.
4. Pre-retirement binary boots on the new SQLite+local store on .93; read-path A/B diff green vs the live PG/B2 instance.
5. Public compose flipped to SQLite + local storage; :latest (Postgres-free, commit 54046de9) deploys cleanly to .93 with no DB-connect errors.
6. .93 Postgres retired only after a final fresh pg_dump -Fc to the NAS; :pre-sqlite tag + NAS dumps retained as cold fallback.

title: Collapse summarizer to map-reduce over chunked JSON extraction
description: Replace the 3-stage pipeline (per-chunk strict-JSON thesis/fact/argument extraction + JSON-repair + dedup/rank call + final summary) with a simple map-reduce: summarize each chunk, then summarize the chunk-summaries into the final markdown. Kill the strict-JSON schema, section-transition tracking, JSON repair loop, and the analyses->payload->parsePayloadAnalyses round-trip. This is the big simplification (summarize.go + services/summarize.go ~1/3 size, fewer LLM round-trips, lower token cost). Verify user-visible markdown summaries are equivalent or better. Depends on facts-removal (qsg) and analysis-table-drop (fdi) landing first so the rewrite starts from a clean base. Also move the whole extraction behind the job queue so it's retried/cancelable and doesn't block the HTTP request.

Prereqs qsg+fdi merged & pushed.
notes: MERGE RECONSTRUCTION (2026-08-07): the map-reduce rewrite actually landed on master 08-04 09:21 via fast-forward (commit 68503d1a became the direct parent of the next master commit a9d6d356), NOT 'not yet merged' as previously recorded. It has been live in origin/master since 08-04 with zero post-merge fixes to services/summarize.go (~3 days, no regression reports). The planned live A/B quality validation on ~10 fixtures was never formally run; Nick accepted implicitly on 2026-08-07 given the clean prod window. Branch xez-summarizer-map-reduce merged back to master 08-07 (caa8e5ec), fully contained.

title: Add HTTP-level test coverage for the OIDC callback handler

Add a test seam around getOIDCProvider (e.g. an overridable provider/exchanger/verifier field) so the callback can be driven end-to-end with a stubbed provider, then assert the happy path issues a JWT redirect and each fail(...) code maps to the right redirect.
