title: Add unique constraint on users.email to prevent duplicate-account signup race
description: Code-review finding surfaced by the OIDC work (Zettelgarden-0ck) but pre-existing and broader. findOrCreateOIDCUser, the GitHub OAuth path (oauth.go), and the password CreateUser path all do existence-check-then-INSERT against the pool with no transaction. A concurrent first-time signup for the same email can create two accounts. The new idx_users_oidc_sub unique partial index safely turns the (provider, sub) race into a clean error, but email has no unique constraint so the email race silently duplicates. OIDC adds another vector on top of GitHub/password. Decision needed: is email globally unique by product rule? If yes, add a unique index (migration 0148) and handle the constraint violation as a clean 'email already exists' error rather than relying on the check-then-insert window. Mind any soft-deleted rows / test accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Unique index on users.email (or a documented decision not to enforce it); concurrent same-email signup cannot create duplicates; full suites green.
close_reason: Landed in commit a30509e9. Unique index idx_users_email added to consolidated schema + SQLite self-heal (guarded: existing duplicate emails warn + defer enforcement instead of crashing boot). Constraint is the backstop for the signup race: CreateUser maps it to a clean 'Email already exists' error (route now surfaces the real message; RegisterPage shows it), GitHub OAuth re-resolves the existing account, findOrCreateOIDCUser re-runs resolution once. Tests: TestCreateUserDuplicateEmail, TestUsersEmailUniqueIndexBlocksRace, TestEnsureSQLiteSchemaUpgrades_EmailIndexIsEnforced/DeferredOnDupes. go test ./..., 565 frontend tests, tsc clean.

title: Add generic OIDC / SSO authentication
description: Implement standards-based OIDC login alongside existing JWT/GitHub/API-key auth. Design: docs/plans/2026-08-03-oidc-authentication-design.md. Phases: (1) backend core — go-oidc + oauth2 deps, OIDCConfig, signed state/nonce cookie, start/callback handlers, routes, schema migration 0147 + schema.sqlite.sql edit; (2) frontend conditional SSO button + env flag (reuse existing ?token= callback); (3) hardening + tests + retrofit GitHub state/CSRF. Open decisions: single vs multi-provider, account-linking UX, sqlite in-place migration path, test IdP.
notes:
PHASE 1+2 IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-03: backend OIDC core (handlers/oidc.go start+callback with PKCE/JWKS/nonce, findOrCreateOIDCUser with auto-link + unverified-email refusal, oauth_state.go signed state cookie + tests), config (OIDCConfig opt-in), routes (/api/auth/oidc/{start,callback}), User model fields, deps (go-oidc/v3 + oauth2), frontend SSO button (VITE_OIDC_ENABLED) + error-code mapping, schema migration 0147 + schema.sqlite.sql. Build + full test suites green (handlers/routes/models; 550 frontend tests). Remaining: e2e against Pocket ID (needs env), Phase 3 GitHub CSRF retrofit.
E2E VALIDATED 2026-08-03 against Pocket ID (id.thesavages.ca). Full login flow works end-to-end on Tailscale dev (frontend :5173, backend :8079). Three integration bugs found & fixed during validation: (1) PKCE — VerifierOption was wrongly passed to AuthCodeURL (must be Exchange only); now sends S256 code_challenge on authorize (commit a26b61b0); (2) nonce — was never sent on the authorize request; now added via SetAuthURLParam (commit f0e621f3); (3) config — OIDC_REDIRECT_URI must point at the backend :8079, not the frontend :5173, and the app has no auto .env loader so the shell must source go-backend/.env-bash. Core OIDC feature COMPLETE. Remaining work split to Zettelgarden-b8b (GitHub OAuth CSRF/state retrofit). Full suites green: go test ./... (17 pkgs), 550 frontend tests, frontend build OK.
CODE REVIEW 2026-08-04 (this session): review of the design doc + full implementation. Verdict: high quality, security model sound (PKCE/JWKS/nonce/state all correct; the two integration bugs found during Pocket ID validation are properly fixed + documented). title: Phase 7a: SQLite cutover + Postgres removal from deploy/config
description:
Execute Phase 7a of docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-design.md: the live cutover (Nick's call; involves app downtime) plus the code/config cleanup that flips SQLite to the default and removes Postgres from the deploy path.

This is the last blocking phase — Phases 0–6 are done (full suite green on SQLite; ETL verified against a copy of live zg_internal: 71 tables / 3,513,290 rows exact / 0 FK violations / idempotent; 560-comparison read-path A/B diff byte-identical; frontend smoke green).

## Part 1 — Cutover procedure (operational; ~30 min downtime)
Follow the Cutover Runbook in the design doc. Iterate against a COPY only; the final run is against the now-static live Postgres.
1. Stop the app (set read-only or halt the go_backend container).
2. Final insurance: `pg_dump -Fc zg_internal > zg_internal_dump-cutover-$(date +%Y%m%d).dump` — store off-host, keep ≥90 days. (Prior insurance dump from gate 1: /home/nick/zg_internal_dump-20260728-124426.dump, 111 MB.)
3. Build the ETL: `cd go-backend && go build -o migrate-pg-to-sqlite ./cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite`.
4. Run the final import against a fresh SQLite file: `./migrate-pg-to-sqlite --pg-dsn '<live DSN>' --sqlite-path ./data/zettelgarden.db`
5. Verification gates (do not proceed unless all green): per-table COUNT(*) PG==SQLite exact; `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` clean; `PRAGMA integrity_check` ok; spot-check a few cards' body md5 + sub-graphs.
6. Flip config: `DB_DRIVER=sqlite`, `SQLITE_PATH=/app/data/zettelgarden.db`. Restart go_backend.
7. Smoke-test in prod: dashboard counts, a card detail, task list, chat history, create+edit a card.

## Part 2 — Code/config cleanup (lands with the flip)
- [ ] Remove the `db` (postgres:16-alpine) service from docker-zettel-run.yml + its `depends_on: service_healthy` on go_backend; mount the SQLite data dir instead.
- [ ] go-backend/.env.example: replace DB_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/NAME with `DB_DRIVER=sqlite` + `SQLITE_PATH=./data/zettelgarden.db`.
- [ ] server/database.go: `sql.Open("postgres", …)` ConnectToDatabase is already only called on the PG branch — confirm dead on the SQLite path; delete ResetDatabase (74c) or gate it on driver=="postgres".
- [ ] scripts/addParentId.go + scripts/computeKeywords.go: both are `//go:build ignore` one-shots; computeKeywords.go is already obsolete (references deleted llms.ComputeCardKeywords). Decide: archive both, or port to the driver abstraction. Recommend archive (they write none of the trigger-affected tables; re-run need is nil post-cutover).
- [ ] Update README.md self-hosting section (lines 62/89/97/100/125 — drop "PostgreSQL + pgvector"; "no external database"). Update AGENTS.md project note (line 4) "expects PostgreSQL" -> "SQLite (file), Typesense, AI keys".
- [ ] Document ongoing backup = `VACUUM INTO 'snapshot-$(date).db'` (NOT raw cp — unsafe under WAL without `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`).
- [ ] Optional fold-in: bn2 (RSS N+1) is independent and can land anytime.

## Notes
- lib/pq STAYS through the cutover window (Decision D6): models/notifications.go, handlers/schemas.go (pq.Error duplicate-key detection), server/database.go, and the ETL tool all still import it. Removal is Phase 7b, ~2 weeks after confirmed-prod.
- Keep Postgres running read-only ≥2 weeks post-cutover as fallback before 7b.
- Post-cutover day-2 backup: a one-time `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` then a `VACUUM INTO`, to establish the ongoing snapshot cadence.

Rehearsal ETL against live PG on .93 (read-only) passed; final ETL with app stopped: pg=3,514,707 sqlite=3,514,707 EXACT, 71 tables, 0 FK violations. Deep verify: integrity_check ok, fk_check empty, 14,544 cards/8,468 tasks/57,896 entities. Backend rebooted on SQLite ('Database connected and migrations completed successfully'); read+write paths confirmed live (scheduled_job_runs accumulating). Postgres on .93 untouched = read-only fallback (>=2 weeks); :pre-sqlite image retained on host for rollback; insurance pg_dump (116MB) on NAS. Originals backed up (.env.pre-sqlite, docker-compose.yml.pre-sqlite). NOTE: committed Dockerfile golang:1.22 -> golang:1.25 (go.mod requires go 1.25.0; the old pin broke the build). title: Phase 6b: build pure-Go ETL tool to import Postgres -> SQLite (cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite)
description:
Execute docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-design.md Phase 6b. With Phase 6a done (full test suite green on SQLite, no Postgres), build the one-time ETL that imports the live ~15k-card Postgres DB into SQLite.

Scope (from the design doc Phase 6b):
- New cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite/ binary: reads live PG tables via lib/pq, writes SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite, in FK-dependency order, preserving PKs verbatim so the graph (entity_card_junction, backlinks, task_dependencies, ...) stays intact.
- Pure-Go -- no CGO fallback. The Phase 1 bulk probe (spike/sqlite_bulk_timing_test.go) measured 15,000 card inserts in 780ms with one tx per insert; batched inserts will be faster.
- Idempotent / re-runnable: prefer INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (pk) DO NOTHING over INSERT OR REPLACE (which fires DELETE+INSERT cascades). Alternative: disable FKs during bulk load, re-enable, then PRAGMA foreign_key_check. Run dozens of times during dev against a COPY of Postgres, never the live DB.
- Domain tables migrated verbatim (cards, card_tags, entities, entity_card_junction, facts, tasks, files, flashcards, summarizations, chat_*, notifications, user_*, rss_*, emails, audit_events, llm_jobs, llm_query_log, etc. -- full list in design doc). System tables (migrations, schema_definitions) rebuilt by the consolidated schema + migration runner, NOT migrated.
- Recommend wholesale migration of audit tables per design Open Question 2.

Highest-stakes remaining phase -- data continuity. Cutover Runbook protections apply (develop against a COPY; final pg_dump insurance; keep Postgres read-only >=2 weeks post-cutover).

Verification gates (Phase 6c) layered on top.

title: Phase 6a: handler pool-vs-test-tx write isolation audit (s.DB vs s.GetDB())
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). Dominant root cause behind the handlers test failures.

Mechanism: handlers.GetDB() returns the rolled-back per-test transaction (h.Server.Tx) in testing mode, but many handler methods write via the raw pool handle s.DB instead, which COMMITS for real. Reads that then go through GetDB() see a snapshot from before the write -> wrong result. Same mechanism leaks rows across tests (test pollution), since pool writes are never rolled back by Teardown.

Concrete confirmed case: handlers/auth.go:197 ResetPasswordRoute does s.DB.Exec('UPDATE users SET password = ...'). Then LoginRoute -> QueryUserByEmail (handlers/users.go:411) reads via s.GetDB() (the test tx, snapshot taken in Setup before the reset) -> sees the OLD password hash -> checkPasswordHash fails -> 401. TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess fails on SQLite; on Postgres MVCC the same staleness applies but the suite may have masked it by ordering. Other handlers using raw s.DB.Exec/Query (auth.go:352/383/413/449/475, plus JobRunner wired with S.DB in handlers/setup_test.go) are suspect.

Knock-on pollution (tests that pass in isolation but fail in the full suite because earlier pool-writes leak): TestGetRelatedCards_Success, TestCreateCardLinkedParentId, TestCreateCardSuccessRecursiveTags, and the 'database is locked' cleanup in TestGetNextChildCardID (pool write during an open tx).

Fix is a systematic audit, NOT a one-line change: route handler writes through GetDB() everywhere a test tx exists; reserve raw s.DB for the few places that genuinely need out-of-transaction access (and make them explicit). Source/JobRunner wiring (setup_test.go) should pass GetDB() too. Verify isolation holds by running the full handlers package (not just single tests).

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a. Largest lever among the remaining failures (~4-5 of the 11).
acceptance_criteria: No handler write path uses raw s.DB where a test-transaction-aware GetDB() is intended; TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess green on SQLite; cross-test card/prefs leakage (Typesense upsert of card 28, etc.) eliminated; documented convention for when raw pool access is legitimately required.
notes:
PART 1 LANDED 2026-07-27 (commit pending): routed two handler write paths through GetDB(): auth.go:197 ResetPasswordRoute (was s.DB.Exec UPDATE users password; the auth-reset test failed because the login read via s.GetDB()/tx couldn't see the pool-committed write) -- fixes TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess. entity.go: all 13 s.DB method-call sites -> s.GetDB() (the entity-card junction INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE writes were the prime pollution suspect for TestGetRelatedCards_Success; reads converted too for consistency). 2 sites kept as s.DB (GetEntities, NewDefaultClient) because their service signatures take *sql.DB, not the interface -- they are reads and don't pollute. Net: handlers failures 8 -> 7, no regressions.

ROOT-CAUSE FINDING (the rest of bto): converting handler WRITES alone is insufficient. The codebase has pervasive s.DB vs s.GetDB() handle INCONSISTENCY in TWO places that must be fixed TOGETHER:
1. TEST LAYER: cards_test.go has 15 sites calling services.CreateCard/UpdateCard(s.DB, ...) directly with the POOL (lines 617,630,742,754,766,778,790,839,851,906,925,938,950,963,994). CreateCard/UpdateCard do all the entity/backlink/fact writes, so pool calls COMMIT and leak across tests (test data is seeded once via sync.Once; pool writes accumulate). This is the source of TestGetRelatedCards_Success pollution (entity_card_junction deletions accumulate until card 1 has no shared entities) AND TestGetNextChildCardID nondeterminism.
2. HANDLER READ PATH: several reads use s.DB (pool), e.g. getNextChildCardID mixes handles within one function -- parent via s.GetDB() (tx) but children via services.GetChildCards(s.DB, ...) (pool). Converting ONLY the test layer breaks: a tx-local create becomes invisible to pool reads (regression observed: TestCheckChunkLinkedOrRelated_Integration broke when only tests were converted).

CORRECT FIX (part 2): convert BOTH together -- all remaining handler s.DB reads+writes to s.GetDB() (the ~80-site audit, minus legitimately-pool-only paths: Stripe webhooks in billing.go, OAuth callbacks in oauth.go, fire-and-forget last_login/last_seen) AND the 15 test-layer services.*(s.DB) calls. Verified directionally that this works but the full sweep needs care (scheduler/background paths where Server.Testing=true but no request tx exists are the risk). Recommend doing it file-by-file with the full suite as the gate.

NOT FIXED YET: TestGetRelatedCards_Success (pollution), TestGetNextChildCardID (handle-mix). The 2 stale status-code expectations (TestCreateCardLinkedParentId GET-expects-201, TestCreateCardSuccessRecursiveTags expects-200-route-returns-201) and 3 RSS network-dependent tests are SEPARATE pre-existing issues, not bto.
close_reason: Part 2 done (2026-07-27): service signatures widened to models.Database (LinkFactToCard, GetUserMemory/UpdateUserMemory, ReorderTaskStatuses refactored off its own Begin() onto handler-managed BeginTx); all handler request-scoped s.DB reads/writes -> s.GetDB(); 15 test-layer services.*(s.DB) calls -> tx; convention documented on Handler.GetDB(). handlers failures 7->0; full suite green on SQLite (no PG). Pre-existing non-SQLite test bugs also fixed (stale 201/200 expectations, getNextChildCardID majority-sep expectation, RSS tests de-networked via injectable services.FeedParser + strconv.Itoa URL fix). See status doc 'Phase 6a complete'.

title: Phase 6a: notification_preferences UPDATE is not an upsert (relies on a trigger that never existed)
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). handlers/notifications.go UpdatePreferences (line ~236) contains the comment 'This is handled by the trigger in the database' — but NO such trigger exists. Migration 0121 only runs a one-time INSERT INTO notification_preferences (user_id) SELECT id FROM users ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; there is no per-user auto-create trigger, and it was never ported to Go in Phase 5 (Phase 5 covered user_stats / llm_jobs / rss notifications, not this).

Consequence: models.UpdateNotificationPreferences does a plain UPDATE ... WHERE user_id = $1. When the user has no prefs row (common — e.g. test users inserted by importTestData, or any user created after the 0121 backfill), the UPDATE affects 0 rows, the handler's 'no rows' retry branch never fires (Exec returns no error), and the subsequent GetNotificationPreferences returns 'sql: no rows' -> handler returns 500 'Failed to get preferences'. This is a latent bug on BOTH Postgres and SQLite, not a SQLite regression.

Fix: make models.UpdateNotificationPreferences an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET ... (works identically on both drivers; the table PK is user_id). Drop the misleading trigger comment and the dead retry branch.

TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess is the failing test. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a.
acceptance_criteria: models.UpdateNotificationPreferences is an upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE) or the handler creates-then-updates; works on both drivers; TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess green on SQLite; the misleading 'trigger' comment removed.
close_reason: Fixed in 1ccaefa8. models.UpdateNotificationPreferences is now INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE (cross-driver). Handler dead 'no rows' branch + misleading trigger comment removed. TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess green on SQLite; models+services packages green; handlers failures 9 -> 8.

title: Phase 6a follow-up: port handlers/facts.go + handlers/entity.go = ANY($1) + array_position to SQLite
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a (2026-07-26). Two production handler sites still use the Postgres array pattern that the services layer was fixed for in the same session:

- handlers/facts.go:808 -- WHERE f.id = ANY($1) ORDER BY array_position($1, f.id), called with pq.Array(factIDs)
- handlers/entity.go:1141 -- WHERE e.id = ANY($1) ORDER BY array_position($1, e.id), called with pq.Array(entityIDs)

The other 7 '= ANY($1)' sites were translated to IN (...) via the new models.InList / models.IntArgs helpers (models/sql.go). These 2 were deferred because they ALSO use 'ORDER BY array_position($1, col)' to preserve the input-slice order, which SQLite has no equivalent for.

Fix: translate '= ANY($1)' to 'IN ' || models.InList(1, len(ids)) (no fixed scalars here, so start at 1), drop the ORDER BY array_position clause, bind via models.IntArgs(ids)..., then reorder the scanned rows app-side to match the input ids order (collect into a map[id]row, emit in input order). Drop the lib/pq import from both files. Verify on both drivers.

These currently fail at runtime on SQLite with 'no such function: ANY' / 'no such function: array_position', contributing to TestGetRelatedCards_Success and the fact-link handler failures. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a.
acceptance_criteria: handlers/facts.go and handlers/entity.go run unchanged on Postgres and SQLite; pq.Array removed from both; the similar-facts / similar-entities result order matches the input ids; lib/pq import dropped from both files; relevant handler tests green on SQLite.
close_reason: Fixed in 07940bd6. handlers/{facts,entity}.go GetSimilar* now use 'IN '+models.InList(1,len(ids)) bound via models.IntArgs(ids)..., with app-side reorder (map-by-id -> emit in ranked input order) replacing ORDER BY array_position. lib/pq dropped from both files. Zero = ANY/array_position/pq.Array remain in non-test Go (grep clean). New idiom smoke test TestSimilarityInListAndAppSideReorder green; all non-handlers packages green; handlers still 8 (these handlers have no direct unit test -- need a Typesense stub).

title: FileVault: support folder/directory drag-and-drop upload
description:
## Context
FileVault drag-and-drop only handles flat files (e.dataTransfer.files). Dragging a folder drops nothing (or an empty file entry). A vault should accept folders and upload their contents recursively, preserving relative paths in the file name where practical.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dragging a folder onto FileVault uploads all contained files recursively (webkitGetAsEntry / webkitdirectory walker)
- Upload progress counts total files across the tree; failures per file reported like today
- Large folder drops show the existing modal progress (file N of M)
- Tests: entry-walker utility unit tested (pure function over mocked entry tree)

title: FileVault: real byte-level upload progress and cancel
description:
## Context
Current upload progress (FileVault + FileUpload) only counts files (1 of N) — for a 50MB file the bar sits at 50% with no movement and no way to cancel. The API uploadFile uses fetch() with FormData; fetch supports ReadableStream request bodies, which enables byte progress via a transform stream, and AbortController for cancel.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Progress bar reflects bytes uploaded (per-file and/or overall) using a streamed request body + upload progress tracking
- Cancel button aborts the in-flight upload (AbortController), cleans up partial state, shows toast
- Backend handles partial/aborted uploads cleanly (no orphaned storage objects or DB rows)
- uploadFile API remains backward compatible for existing callers (card page, FilesTab)

title: FileVault: duplicate fetch on mount and on every debounced search
description:
## Context
FileVault.tsx has overlapping data-fetch effects: the mount effect (setDocumentTitle + fetchFiles) and the deps-driven effect [currentPage, filetypeFilter, unlinkedOnly, sortBy, sortOrder] both fire on initial render -> 2 requests. Debounced search calls setSearchTerm + setCurrentPage(1) in one batch, so the deps effect and the [searchTerm] effect both fire -> 2 requests per search. Redundant network calls, quota-bar flicker, and race risk (older response can land last).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open FileVault with network tab open — GET /files fires twice on mount
2. Type in the search box and pause — two GET /files requests per debounce tick

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exactly one GET /files on mount and one per (debounced) filter/sort change
- Refactor to a single fetch effect keyed on all inputs (page, search, filetype, unlinked, sort, order); keep refreshFiles behavior
- Existing smoke test still passes
close_reason: Fixed: filetype: syntax parsed into filetype param (util + tests); keyboard Enter clicks real download link, Delete removes highlighted row with confirm, no stale closures (tests); uploads preserve current query; single fetch effect (mount-call-count asserted in smoke test)

title: FileVault: uploading clears active search and filters
description:
## Context
FileVault.tsx refreshFiles effect (`if (refreshFiles) fetchFiles(1, '', '', false, sortBy, sortOrder)`) refetches with cleared search/filters. Both the header upload button (FileUpload sets refreshFiles) and drag-and-drop uploads (handleDrop calls setRefreshFiles(true)) trigger this, so any active search/filter/unlinked toggle silently resets after an upload. The newly uploaded file may also not match the active filter, making the reset doubly confusing.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open FileVault, search for 'quarterly' (or enable Unlinked Only)
2. Upload a file via the button or drag-and-drop
3. Search box text stays but results reset to unfiltered list (and Clear-all chip disappears until debounce)

## Acceptance Criteria
- After an upload, the current search term + filters + page are preserved when refetching
- Newly uploaded file appears if it matches the active filter; no full reset of user context
close_reason: Fixed: filetype: syntax parsed into filetype param (util + tests); keyboard Enter clicks real download link, Delete removes highlighted row with confirm, no stale closures (tests); uploads preserve current query; single fetch effect (mount-call-count asserted in smoke test)

title: Desktop file keychain: write secrets with 0600 permissions
description:
Code review of Zettelgarden-77j found desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs CredentialStore::store writes the ZG_KEYCHAIN_FILE JSON with std::fs::write, which under a default umask (022) yields 0644 — the session JWT is world-readable on disk. The file backend is opt-in and headless-only (documented 'not encrypted'), but a credentials file should be 0600 regardless.

Fix: open with OpenOptions .mode(0o600) (or chmod after write); same trait at settings.json write (line ~198) is lower priority (non-secret data).

title: Sync harness: add delete-race + feed-pagination convergence scenarios
description:
Follow-up from the independent subagent review of Zettelgarden-xre (Phase 1b harness). The delete-race case (offline delete vs concurrent edit) was added as scenario 07 and caught a real ghost-row bug (is_deleted 0/1 vs boolean) which is now fixed in engine.ts (rowIsDeleted truthiness + drop the mirror row when the adopted server conflict data says deleted).

Still NOT covered by the harness:
1. Feed pagination: the changes feed pages at syncFeedPageSize (500, handlers/sync.go) with has_more + cursor contract. No scenario pushes >500 rows, so a pagination regression (e.g. cursor advance, has_more handling in engine pull()) would not be caught by CI. Suggest a scenario that creates ~510 rows across devices, settles, and asserts convergence + a server-side row count.
2. Tombstone application on the plain offline-delete path is exercised implicitly in scenario 07 (B's pull skips the tombstone while pending), but a dedicated 'delete propagates via feed' assertion (A deletes offline, B pulls the tombstone with NO pending edit, row disappears) is only covered by engine unit tests (mock), not the live backend.
3. Batch >10MiB or >500 changes in one push (syncPushMaxBytes guard) — untested end-to-end.

Acceptance: two new scenarios (pagination + delete-propagates) or one combined; green against the live backend; exit non-zero on divergence.
close_reason: Fixed in 811c12dd. Scenario 08 (delete-propagates): A deletes offline and pushes the tombstone; B with NO pending edit sees the row disappear purely from the feed pull (previously mock-only). Scenario 09 (feed-pagination): 510 changes in ONE push batch + paginated pull across two pages (syncFeedPageSize=500) with assertions on pushed==510, pulled==510, server count 511, full convergence. >10MiB byte guard branch covered by the MaxBytesReader by construction. Gates: npm run harness 9/9 green against live backend; sync-engine unit tests 40/40.

title: DashboardPage hardcodes user_id: 0 for recent cards (subagent review N7)
description:

title: Tag rename tombstone: soft-delete the renamed-away name (v1 sync policy refinement)
description:
Third-pass review of the sync design (docs/plans/2026-08-07-mobile-desktop-sync-app-design.md, item 1) recommended: for tag rename under name-keyed merge, treat rename as a normal upsert of the new name AND soft-delete the renamed-away name's row, so a concurrent offline create of the old name resurrects the tombstone instead of creating a fresh row. Not implemented.

Phase 1b harness (Zettelgarden-xre) validated the CURRENT behavior: rename-vs-create (A renames work->tasks while B creates a new 'work' offline) converges deterministically — one live 'tasks' (A's row) + one live 'work' (B's fresh row) on every device and the server. Observable convergence is identical with or without the tombstone, so the harness passes either way; the tombstone is a policy refinement for: (a) keeping the deleted-name identity/uuid stable across a rename+recreate cycle, (b) matching REST CreateTag's resurrect semantics for the renamed-away name.

Implementing it requires: applyTagUpsert + REST EditTag to insert a tombstone row (is_deleted=true, new sync_uuid, old name) when the name changes; the name-keyed merge must prefer live rows over tombstones (the merge lookup currently QueryRows an arbitrary row when both exist); emit/retention decisions for the tombstone row (snapshot excludes deleted rows, so clients never see it unless they recreate it). Coordinate with the tag-merge lost-edit accounting.
close_reason: Implemented in b3dfd846. applyTagUpsert UPDATE path now tombstones the renamed-away name (fresh uuid, is_deleted=true, never emitted; skipped if a live row or tombstone already holds the name, inserted before the rename applies so failure aborts the change); name-keyed merge prefers live rows over tombstones (ORDER BY is_deleted ASC, id). REST EditTag is dead code (no rename route), so the sync path is the only rename path. Tests: Go TestSyncPushTagRenameTombstone (tombstone row + fresh uuid, B's create merged onto tombstone uuid, exactly one live work + one live tasks) + harness scenario 10 (rename-vs-create) — verified red on pre-fix code, green with fix. Gates: go test ./... green, gofmt clean, sync-engine 40/40, harness 10/10. Harness README policy-gap section replaced.

title: s2l follow-ups: sync/REST structured_data-without-schema divergence, EditPage per-save fetch, dead []string case
description:
Cleanup follow-ups from the code review of Zettelgarden-s2l (required schema fields). Three small items:

1. [divergence] Sync push path accepts structured_data WITHOUT schema_id silently; REST rejects with 400 "structured_data requires schema_id to be specified" (handlers/cards.go else-if). The s2l goal was "same user intent, same outcome by transport" — this edge is still divergent. Fix: in services/sync_apply.go applyCardUpsert, when data.CardSchemaID == nil and data.StructuredData is non-nil/non-empty, reject with a ValidationError mirroring REST. Note: normal UI flow sends both or neither (frontend clears data on schema change), so severity is low, but the divergence is real.

2. [perf] EditPage.handleSaveCard calls fetchSchema() on EVERY save to validate required fields. CardSchemaSection already loads the full schema list via fetchSchemas() on mount; the save path could reuse that cached list instead of an extra round-trip per save. Fix: lift the schema list into EditPage state (or a tiny schema cache), validate from memory, keep the server as fallback.

3. [nit] services/schema_validation.go isEmptyRequiredValue has a dead "[]string" case — json.Unmarshal into map[string]interface{} only ever produces []interface{}, so []string can never occur. Delete the case (or keep as documentation of intent; prefer deleting for clarity).

All three are small and can land as one PR or three tiny ones. Coordinate with the schema-removal bug bead (Zettelgarden-276) if fixing the else-if guard there touches the same code.

## Acceptance
Sync push with non-empty structured_data but no schema_id returns 400 with a message (mirrors REST); EditPage validates required fields without an extra fetch per save (tests still green); isEmptyRequiredValue has no dead []string branch. Go + frontend suites green.
close_reason: Fixed in 552103a3. zt3: keychain file written 0600 (unix; cfg-not-unix fallback) + test asserts mode; 9p7: smoke.sh cargo build failure now fatal (no || true, stale binary can't pass); 6mj: launch 2 stops the backend, session scenario asserts keychain auth + mirror render + no-connection indicator (Offline or Sync error — engine shows Sync error when machine online but server unreachable); 23n: e2e_report refuses outside ZG_E2E=1, CredentialStore explicit loaded flag (+ regression test), dead smoke.ts line removed, README lists python3. a1u: sync push rejects non-empty structured_data without schema_id (400, mirrors REST) + new handler test; isEmptyRequiredValue dead []string case removed; fetchSchemas session cache (invalidated on create/update/delete) + EditPage validates from cache. Gates: go test ./... green, cargo test 6 green, tsc/format/892 vitest/build green, desktop E2E smoke passed end-to-end. Note: existing TestSyncPushSchemaValidationRejectsInvalidStructuredData third assertion still passes via the shared-test-tx rollback wrong path (pre-existing harness footgun, out of scope).

title: REST write paths emit sync_log non-atomically (row commits, emit may fail silently)
description: Code-review follow-up (P3-3): the REST write paths (CreateCard/UpdateCard/DeleteCard etc.) call emitRowChange on the pool handle after the mutation — a separate transaction from the row write. A failed emit leaves the row committed but invisible to sync, and a client retry of the 500 can create a second row (new uuid). The sync push path is properly transactional (v5b.3); the REST path is not. This matches the documented Phase 0a convention (services/sync.go) but is a real gap; fixing requires threading a transaction through the REST handlers or accepting + documenting.
notes: Subagent review of a36bef72 caught + fixed in c5489dc6: (1) CompleteAndScheduleTask swallowed the completion error (incl. emit failures) -> now propagates so the tx rolls back new task + completion together; (2) RestoreCardToAuditEventRoute was a missed emit-capable route -> wrapped; (3) TestCreateCardRouteRollsBackWhenEmitFails proves production rollback via a forced sync_log trigger (verified red on pre-fix code). Known limitation (documented, follow-up candidate): Typesense upsert/delete runs inside the route tx, holding the SQLite write lock across the HTTP call — same as the existing sync push path; mitigation (post-commit Typesense or SQLITE_BUSY retry) deferred.
close_reason: Fixed in a36bef72. Added commitTx/rollbackTx helpers (commit in production, no-op in the test harness; rollback no-ops in tests so error paths no longer poison the shared test tx). Wrapped all primary REST write routes so the mutation + its sync_log emit commit in ONE transaction: cards (create/update/delete/article), structured data (update/patch/clear), tasks (create/update incl recurring/delete/complete+schedule/update-parent/reorder/subtask), task status delete (incl. reassignment emits), tags (create/delete). Handler methods now take the caller's tx; task tag re-derivation moved after commit (derived rows, own emits, no orphaned junctions on commit failure). Documented out of scope: background emitters (reminder service, recurring generation, registration seed) — no REST retry-duplication surface. New test asserts create/update/delete emit exactly upsert:1/upsert:2/delete:3 through the route+tx path. Gates: go test ./... green, gofmt clean, sync harness 9/9, desktop E2E smoke passed end-to-end.

title: Retry matcher requires exactly version == base+1 (identical content beyond that conflicts)
description: Code-review follow-up (P3-1): services/sync_apply.go retryMatchesCurrent only treats a stale push as an idempotent retry when version == base+1, even when the pushed payload is byte-identical to the current row. Two devices setting the same value, or a retry arriving after another edit that happened to produce identical content, reports a spurious conflict + lost edit. Deliberate (conservative) but arguably wrong for the identical-content case; decide whether to relax the guard to payload-match-only.
close_reason: Fixed in 8ba5aa9d. idp: applyCardUpsert now mirrors REST's checkIsCardIDUnique — CREATE-path duplicate card_id is MERGED onto the winner (adopt the winner's uuid, like the tag name-merge, so no ghost row re-conflicts on every edit); UPDATE-path rename to an owned card_id is a conflict (lost edit). Empty card_id exempt. merged() helper generalized to take the collection. dsd: retryMatchesCurrent relaxed to payload-match-only (no version==base+1 guard) — identical content is idempotent-applied even when the row advanced past base+1; genuinely different stale content still conflicts. Tests: TestSyncPushRejectsDuplicateCardID + TestSyncPushIdenticalContentStaleBaseNoConflict. Gates: go test ./... green, sync-engine 40/40, harness 9/9.

title: Schema table polish: add-card-from-table, CSV export, field reorder
description:
Schema assessment (2026-08-08, SchemaPage.tsx + SchemaTablePage.tsx review). The schema feature is functionally complete (7 field types, {{schema:}} markdown embed, search filter, inline table editing) but three table-level UX gaps make it feel less like a real data tool:

1. Add card from table: SchemaTablePage has no way to create a new card pre-attached to this schema. Expected: an 'Add card' / '+ New row' action in the table header that goes to /app/card/new with the schema pre-selected (reuse the existing EditPage new-card path + card_schema_id), then the table refreshes to include it.
2. CSV export: no way to export the current (filtered) table view. Expected: export the visible/filtered rows as CSV (title + card_id + structured fields), honoring current filters; low effort, high utility for a self-hosted tool.
3. Field reorder: SchemaDialog (components/schemas/SchemaDialog.tsx) can add/remove/update fields but cannot reorder them (no move up/down or drag). Field order is what the editor displays top-to-bottom on cards, so ordering matters. Expected: move up/down buttons (cheap) or drag (nice); persisted order already implied by fields array order in schema_definitions JSON.

## Do
- All three are independent; can land as one PR or separate small PRs.
- Coordinate: 'add card from table' interacts with the v5b sync pinned-table work (cards only) and the fv3 data-layer swap only if it lands after fv3; otherwise the current fetch() path is fine.
- Tests: table page renders the new actions; CSV export produces expected columns; reorder buttons update field order and persist.

## Non-goals
- No pivot/group-by/rollup views (Notion-database parity is out of scope).
- No schema-level sharing or templates.
acceptance_criteria: Table header offers 'Add card' that opens card/new pre-attached to the schema and the table shows the new row after save; CSV export of the filtered table view downloads with title/card_id/structured fields; SchemaDialog supports reordering fields and the persisted order renders top-to-bottom on cards; frontend tests cover all three; suites green.
close_reason: All three features landed: (1) SchemaTablePage header now has Add Card -> /app/card/new?schema=<id>; EditPage reads the ?schema= param and pre-attaches it to the new card (metadata rail shows the schema + structured fields). (2) Export CSV downloads the current filtered/sorted table view as <slug>-cards.csv with card_id/title/structured-field columns (RFC 4180 escaping, multi-select joined). (3) SchemaDialog field editors gained move up/down buttons (disabled at edges); persisted order = fields array order on save. 19 new frontend tests (schemaCsv util 9, SchemaDialog 4, SchemaTablePage 4, EditPage 2) + existing 763 all green; tsc + production build pass.

title: Unify ViewPage + EditPage into one card route with click-to-edit body (Obsidian-style live edit)
description:
Product idea (2026-08-08, Nick): merge pages/cards/EditPage.tsx + ViewPage.tsx into a single /app/card/:id experience — view by default, click the body to start editing in place, click away / Escape / explicit save to return to view. Obsidian/Notion-style.

## Why it's feasible (verified in code)
- CardBodyTextArea already has an internal preview mode (textarea <-> ReactMarkdown toggle) — the view half of the toggle already lives in the editor component.
- ViewPage already saves inline (handleSaveCard -> saveExistingCard -> setViewCard) and CardBody accepts onSave, so the view side already mutates.
- useRightPaneTab (?pane=) is already shared between both pages.
- Both pages already implement the same closable/resizable right-rail pattern.

## What the work is
1. Single route /app/card/:id with isEditing state (keep /app/card/new separate: templates, draft restore, URL-fill, title suggestion, nextCardId).
2. Unify the two data-loading paths: useViewPageContainer (View) vs EditPageContent.fetchCard + the CardEditorProvider/EditorUIProvider/EditorMessagesProvider context stack (Edit). Decide whether the editor contexts survive or get folded into the merged page.
3. Reconcile right-rail tabs: View has Links/Metadata/Entities/Files; Edit has Metadata/Links/Files.
4. Save semantics decision: explicit save (current) vs save-on-blur vs autosave. Must reconcile with optimistic invalidation + React Query cache in the fv3 data-layer work.
5. Mobile: merge ViewMobileLayout + MobileTopBar paths.

## Sequencing (IMPORTANT)
GATE ON Zettelgarden-fv3 (Phase 2b desktop data-layer swap, ~28 files incl. both pages). Doing this merge now means redoing it against the local-SQLite layer; doing it after fv3 means refactoring once on a stable data layer. Recommend: file now, start after fv3 lands. Also coordinate with a5q.6 smoke tests (both pages are on the smoke-test list) — merged page needs updated smoke coverage, not two separate ones.

## Non-goals
- No changes to markdown rendering, wiki-links, or the right-rail components themselves.
- /app/card/new stays a separate edit-only flow.
acceptance_criteria: /app/card/:id renders in view mode by default; clicking the body switches to edit; edits save via the chosen semantics and return to view without losing the right-rail tab state; /app/card/new still works (templates/draft/URL-fill); mobile layout merged; EditPage.test.tsx + ViewPage smoke coverage updated for the merged page; all suites green.

description:

title: Desktop signed CI builds (v5b Phase 2 exit criterion: macOS notarization + Windows signing)
description:
Design docs/plans/2026-08-07-mobile-desktop-sync-app-design.md Phase 2 exit criteria require 'signed CI builds per OS'. Current state: .github/workflows/desktop.yml only runs 'npx tauri build --no-bundle' (compile check, unsigned artifacts). No issue tracks production signing/notarization for the Tauri desktop app (Zettelgarden-c5b, desktop/).

Scope:
- macOS: Developer ID Application signing + Apple notarization (tauri-action or tauri-build notarization step; needs APPLE_CERTIFICATE/APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY/APPLE_ID creds as repo secrets)
- Windows: code-signing cert (signtool via tauri-action; cert + password secrets) — optional if no Windows cert available; document decision
- Linux: AppImage/AppImageHub or deb signing decision (lowest priority)
- Upload artifacts (dmg/msi/AppImage) to GitHub Releases on tag (tauri-action release step)

Gate: this only matters at ship time — it does NOT block fv3 (2b data-layer swap) or c6l (3a). Flag as follow-up needing Nick's decision on cert provisioning (Apple Developer account + Windows cert purchase).

description:

title: Desktop shell hardening: keychain shim gaps + CSP/bridge exposure (c5b follow-up)
description:
Found in code review of v5b (c5b). Two hardening items on the Tauri shell:

1) preload.js localStorage->keychain shim: (a) writes are fire-and-forget promises - a quick logout-then-login can race set/delete keychain ops out of order, leaving the keychain state wrong; (b) localStorage.clear()/key()/length pass through the Proxy to the real storage and bypass the keychain - the web app does not call clear() today, but the shim should override it defensively (a future clear() would leave the token in the keychain, silently keeping a user logged in after 'logout').

2) tauri.conf.json has csp:null + withGlobalTauri:true, and the app has a configurable server URL. Any XSS in the bundled SPA gets unrestricted access to the __TAURI__ bridge including get_secret (reads the JWT from the OS keychain). Recommend a CSP ('self' + configured server origin) and consider gating the secret commands (e.g. confirm the request originates from the bundled origin).,
acceptance_criteria: localStorage.clear()/key()/length are overridden to include keychain keys (unit test in the shim or a manual spec); logout-then-login does not leave stale keychain state; a CSP is set for the bundled SPA that does not break the configured server API origin. Desktop tests green.
close_reason: preload.js: per-key serialized keychain writes (logout-then-login can't reorder), clear()/key()/length now include keychain keys, shim core extracted to a UMD createShim with a new vitest suite (5 tests). tauri.conf.json: withGlobalTauri=false (page never sees __TAURI__; only the preload's __TAURI_INTERNALS__ invoke reaches get_secret) + strict CSP (script-src 'self', connect-src self+http(s) for the configurable server, ws for dev HMR). Verified: shim tests green, cargo build + rust tests green, app launches under xvfb with no CSP/preload errors. Landed 632050bb.

title: Engine cleanup: exponential backoff is dead code; pull() has a dead cursor branch
description:
Found in code review of v5b (nqx), sync-engine/src/engine.ts:

1) Scheduler 'exponential backoff' never delays anything: start(intervalMs) fires the timer at the fixed intervalMs, and on failure only computes backoffMs = min(backoffMs*2, maxBackoffMs) which is never used as the next timer delay. Auto-sync retries at constant frequency regardless of repeated failure. Either honor it (setTimeout chain with backoffMs) or remove the dead state.

2) pull() contains a per-entry dead branch: 'if (entry.row_uuid) { cursor = Math.max(cursor, page.cursor); }' - page.cursor is constant across the page and setCursor(page.cursor) already runs unconditionally at the end of the transaction. Remove or make the intent explicit.,
acceptance_criteria: Engine auto-sync backs off exponentially after repeated failures (test with a failing transport asserting increasing intervals, or the dead state removed with a comment). pull() has no dead branches (code coverage or review). Vitest green.
close_reason: start() chains setTimeout: steady state at intervalMs, failures double the wait up to maxBackoffMs (reset on success) — the previously dead backoffMs now drives real delays. pull() hoists cursor = page.cursor after the page transaction, removing the per-entry branch that hid multi-page cursor advancement. Fake-timer test asserts 1000->2000->4000 doubling + maxBackoffMs cap. vitest 22/22, tsc green; landed cdfdbc4b.

title: Tag name-merge discards the losing device's edit without counting a lost edit
description:
Found in code review of v5b (tsv/nqx). When a pushed tag merges onto an existing same-named server row and the server row wins (ch.BaseVersion <= mergedVersion), the losing device's offline edit (e.g. color change, rename) is silently discarded and the push returns status=merged with lost_edits unchanged. The client adopts the surviving row's data with no indication its edit was dropped.

Data converges (one server tag, uuid adopted) which is correct, but the 'lost-edit count returned' promise is incomplete for the merge case. Relevant to Phase 4's conflict-inbox UX (surface discarded-edit counts).

Fix direction: decide whether merge-loss counts as a lost edit (likely yes when the pushed data differs from the surviving row) and surface it in the push response / engine summary.,
acceptance_criteria: A merged tag whose pushed data differs from the surviving server row reports the loss (lost_edits increment or a per-result flag the client can surface); a merge where the pushed data is identical reports no loss. Handler + engine tests cover both. Policy documented in the sync design doc.
close_reason: A tag name-merge that discards a differing offline edit (name/color/is_deleted differ from the surviving row) now increments lost_edits via tagPushDiffersFromRow; identical-to-row merges (same-color concurrent create, identical retry) report no loss. MockServer mirrors the policy; engine summary surfaces summary.lostEdits. Handler + engine tests cover both. Policy + differing-retry re-count limitation documented in the design doc Conflict Policy. go test ./... + vitest 23/23 green; landed 91694382.

title: Eliminate remaining act() warnings (~78 across ~10 test files)

title: Generalize SQLite incremental schema migrations beyond the hand-maintained self-heal list
description: Surfaced by the 2026-08-04 OIDC prod outage ('no such column: oidc_provider'). The SQLite migration path only applies the consolidated schema/sqlite/schema.sqlite.sql for FRESH builds; the numbered Postgres migrations in ./schema (e.g. 0147-add-oidc-subject.sql) are never scanned on SQLite and use non-portable syntax (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, COMMENT ON) anyway. So existing/pre-cutover SQLite DBs had no way to pick up new columns except a manual ALTER. Immediate fix landed (commit pending): server/database.go ensureSQLiteSchemaUpgrades() runs idempotently on every boot and back-fills the oidc_provider/oidc_sub columns + idx_users_oidc_sub index, guarded by table/column-existence checks. Remaining work (this issue): replace the hand-maintained upgrade list with a real incremental-migration mechanism for SQLite — e.g. a SQLite-specific migrations subdir scanned by RunMigrations containing idempotent, SQLite-safe statements, or a small framework that guards each ALTER. Until then, any new NOT-NULL-on-add or type-change column (which SQLite ADD COLUMN can't express) would need a rebuild or a one-off. Design ref: docs/plans/2026-08-03-oidc-authentication-design.md Database/Schema section.
close_reason: Addressed at the right scope (2026-08-04): schema-sync drift test landed (CI-guarding the self-heal list against the consolidated schema) + Postgres retired (removing the cross-engine parity pressure). Full numbered-migrations framework deferred as overkill for a single-engine single-user app; reopen if drift recurs or a NOT-NULL-on-add/type-change column is needed. See docs/plans/2026-08-04-sqlite-schema-sync-and-pg-retirement.md.

comments.author: Nick Savage
comments.text: Resolution (2026-08-04): decided to DEFER the full numbered-migrations framework and instead ship the right-scoped fix for a single-engine, single-user app: (1) a schema-sync drift test (TestSelfHealListMatchesSchemaDelta in server/database_sqlite_upgrade_test.go) that fails CI if the self-heal list and the consolidated schema diverge — this guards the exact OIDC-class gap that prompted this issue; the self-heal upgrades list was hoisted to a package var (sqliteSelfHealUpgrades) so the test and runner share one definition, with a frozen pre-self-heal users-column baseline. (2) Retired Postgres (epic Zettelgarden-c7j Phase 7b): lib/pq dropped, runtime collapsed to SQLite-only, 148 numbered PG migrations archived — which removes the cross-engine parity pressure that motivated a heavier mechanism. The hand-maintained self-heal list is now CI-guarded, which is sufficient here. Reopen / escalate to the framework if (a) drift recurs despite the test, or (b) a NOT-NULL-on-add or type-change column is needed (SQLite ADD COLUMN can't express those; they'd require a rebuild or a one-off). Design + follow-ups: docs/plans/2026-08-04-sqlite-schema-sync-and-pg-retirement.md. Full Go suite green.

title: findOrCreateOIDCUser: handle already-linked-with-different-sub case explicitly
description: Code-review finding from Zettelgarden-0ck. In the email-match branch, findOrCreateOIDCUser runs: UPDATE users SET oidc_provider=$1, oidc_sub=$2 ... If the matched account already has a DIFFERENT non-empty oidc_sub, the UPDATE affects 0 rows and the function returns the existing user with no error and no link — a silent no-op that could mask an odd state. Harmless for a single provider today, but should at least be logged (and ideally surface as an explicit error or decision) so the state is observable.

title: Add ETL->app read regression test (catch jsonb/array storage-format drift)
description: The cutover shipped a latent bug: the ETL stored jsonb as TEXT (string) and PG arrays as JSON, while the app reads jsonb as []byte (json.RawMessage, which cannot scan a Go string) and arrays via pq.StringArray ({a,b} text). The test suite missed it because every DB test inserts via the app (BLOB storage), never via ETL-style TEXT storage; gate-3 read-path diff also used app-style data. Add a regression test that (a) inserts a cards.structured_data / starred_searches.search_config / notifications.filter_tags row using the ETL's normalizeValue output (or a raw string bind mimicking it) into a SQLite file, then reads it through the real services.GetFullCard / models scan, asserting no scan error. This pins the contract that ETL-produced storage is app-readable. File under c7j; surfaced by the 2026-07-29 cutover scan-error incident.
acceptance_criteria: A test reproduces the ETL storage shape and confirms the app read path (GetFullCard structured_data, starred search search_config, notification filter_tags) scans without error; fails if normalizeValue ever regresses to TEXT/JSON storage.
close_reason: TestETLStorageIsAppReadable + TestBuggyETLStorageFailsScan pin the ETL storage contract (jsonb as []byte BLOB, arrays as {a,b} text) through the real read paths on the modernc driver; buggy TEXT/JSON shapes fail to scan, reproducing the incident error. Landed d3bf2bb8.

title: Phase 2 follow-up: drop habits/habit_logs from consolidated SQLite schema (mirror migration 0144)
description:
Surfaced by the first live ETL run (Phase 6c gate 1, 2026-07-28). The live dev Postgres DB no longer has habits/habit_logs: migration 0144-remove-habits-feature.sql dropped them (0131/0132 added them). But the consolidated SQLite schema (schema/sqlite/schema.sqlite.sql, generated from the 2026-07-25 pg_dump snapshot which predated 0144 being applied to that snapshot) still contains both tables, so they show up as 'SQLite-only skipped' (2 tables) in the ETL's PG∩SQLite intersection.

Impact is nil: no Go code references habits (grep finds nothing), the ETL correctly skips them (no PG data -> no data loss), and they'd just be empty tables after cutover. But it is real schema drift: the consolidated schema is out of sync with production.

Fix: mirror 0144 in the SQLite world -- either remove the habits/habit_logs CREATE TABLE (+ any indexes) from schema.sqlite.sql, or append a SQLite-side drop migration, so a fresh SQLite install matches the post-0144 PG schema. Verify by re-running the ETL and confirming the 'SQLite-only skipped' set is empty.

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j. Not a blocker for cutover (Phase 7a cleanup is also acceptable).
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated SQLite schema no longer contains habits or habit_logs; ETL run reports 0 SQLite-only-skipped tables; go test ./... still green.
close_reason: Closed 2026-07-28: removed habits + habit_logs CREATE TABLEs and their 6 indexes from schema/sqlite/schema.sqlite.sql (mirrors PG migration 0144-remove-habits-feature.sql). No Go code references habits (grep clean); the only FK was habit_logs->habits (internal). Table count 72 -> 71; TestConsolidatedSchemaLoads green (FK + integrity check ok); full go test ./... green; go build ok. A fresh SQLite install now matches post-0144 production; the ETL's SQLite-only-skipped set will be empty on the next run.

title: Phase 5 follow-up: collapse N+1 in syncRSSArticleNotificationsByPredicate (services/rss_notifications.go)
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 5 review (2026-07-26). services/rss_notifications.go syncRSSArticleNotificationsByPredicate() (used by MarkRSSFeedAsRead and MarkRSSFolderAsRead in services/rss.go) issues one GetRSSArticleByID SELECT per matched article -- an N+1. The original PG trigger had the full row in hand and fired once per row, so this is a small perf regression. Acceptable at single-user scale, but a large feed/folder mark-read would feel it.

Fix is small: change the helper to SELECT the full rss_articles columns (not just id) in its single predicate query, hydrate models.RSSArticle directly, and call SyncRSSArticleNotification without the per-row GetRSSArticleByID round-trip. Keep it best-effort (log + continue).

Not a blocker for Phase 6a. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.

close_reason: syncRSSArticleNotificationsByPredicate now SELECTs full rows in one predicate query (shared scanRSSArticle helper with GetRSSArticleByID); regression test asserts exactly 1 rss_articles SELECT for a 25-article feed mark-read. Landed 6f18859f.

title: Phase 7a: drop or modernize PG-only ResetDatabase in server/database.go
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 1-5 SQLite review (2026-07-26). server/database.go ResetDatabase() is still fully PG-specific: CASCADE on every DROP TABLE, SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, DROP TABLE ... CASCADE, etc. It is NOT on the SQLite code path (SQLite uses bootstrap + RunMigrations), so it is harmless today, but it is a latent inconsistency that will confuse readers post-cutover.

Action: as part of Phase 7a (cleanup & rollout), either (a) delete ResetDatabase entirely if nothing calls it on the SQLite path, or (b) gate it on S.Driver == 'postgres' and add a SQLite equivalent (or a no-op). While there, confirm no callers remain that assume PG semantics.

Not a blocker for Phase 6a. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.
acceptance_criteria: ResetDatabase either removed or driver-gated; no PG-only SQL remains on the SQLite boot path; backend still boots on both drivers.
close_reason: Done 2026-07-29 (Phase 7a Part 2): ResetDatabase deleted from server/database.go (it was PG-only: CASCADE/SERIAL/DROP...CASCADE) and its only call site removed from tests/conftest.go. Stale comment referencing it also fixed. Full suite green on SQLite (go test ./... exit 0). ConnectToDatabase (the postgres boot path) remains until Phase 7b per D6.

title: file_count in user_stats never decrements (files only soft-deleted)
description:
Pre-existing bug surfaced during SQLite Phase 5 scoping (2026-07-25). The user_stats.file_count counter only ever INCREMENTS: the old PG trigger trg_files_delete fired AFTER DELETE (hard delete), but the Go server only ever soft-deletes files (UPDATE files SET is_deleted=true in handlers/files.go DeleteFileRoute). So file_count grows monotonically and overcounts over time.

Decision (Nick, 2026-07-25): leave current behavior as-is for now; do NOT fix as part of Phase 5. Track here. When fixing, decrement file_count in the Go files soft-delete path (and consider whether hard-deletes should ever happen).
close_reason: Added DecrementUserFileCount (floored at 0) and wired it into DeleteFileRoute after the storage delete succeeds (consistent with the is_deleted rollback). Tests: TestUserStatsCounters floor case + TestDeleteFile asserts counter 1->0 through the real route. Landed 8638df54.

title: FileVault: warn on duplicate uploads (same name+size or content hash)
description:
## Context
Uploading the same file twice creates two independent vault entries with no warning — easy to do accidentally via drag-drop + button, and storage quota makes duplicates costly. A content hash or name+size heuristic can detect likely duplicates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- On upload, backend (or client) detects an existing file with same content hash (or same name+size as a fallback) for the user
- UI prompts (confirm dialog or toast with option) before/after creating the duplicate: 'A file with identical content already exists — upload anyway / skip'
- Detection cost is acceptable (hash computed client-side before upload, or backend hashes on ingest and checks)
- Tests cover the dedupe check path

title: Test-quality nits in new a5q test files (dead fixture field, weak refetch assertion, brittle undefined-arg assertion)
description:
Why: code review of the a5q test additions found three small quality issues that will slowly erode the suite's signal:
1. src/hooks/queries/useCards.test.tsx 'card sub-resource hooks' it.each cases[] carries an unused 'url' field (dead data; tests assert the mock was called with the id, not the URL).
2. useCards.test.tsx 'refetches when search params change' asserts toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('second', expect.anything() x11, undefined) — the 11 anything() args make the assertion nearly vacuous; the file already has a full-assertion defaults test, so a shared expected-params helper would make this precise without duplication.
3. src/api/cards.test.ts starCard asserts toHaveBeenCalledWith('/cards/5/star', undefined) — asserting an explicit undefined second arg is brittle; if the implementation stops passing it, the test breaks for the wrong reason (or silently passes if impl adds a body).

Do:
- Drop the unused url field (or assert on it)
- Replace expect.anything() x11 with the concrete mapped params (extract a shared expectation)
- Relax the starCard assertion to not require the explicit undefined arg (e.g. objectContaining on path only, or expect.arrayContaining)

Acceptance: all three nits addressed; suite stays green.

title: Phase 5 follow-up: harden userstats addAmount $2-twice param reuse against driver version bumps
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 5 review (2026-07-26). services/userstats.go addAmount() references $2 twice in one statement (once in VALUES, once in the ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET) and binds a single positional arg. modernc.org/sqlite v1.54.0 and lib/pq both correctly bind the same arg to both occurrences (verified by services/userstats_sqlite_test.go which accumulates to ~0.20 llm_cost / 750 revenue), so this works today on both drivers.

The concern is purely future-proofing: reuse of a numbered param is the one construct in the SQLite migration that is most sensitive to a modernc version bump changing how repeated numbered params are bound.

Options if it ever breaks (low priority): (a) bind the amount twice from the caller side ($2 and $3), or (b) switch to a named param via sql.Named. No action needed today -- this issue exists purely as a breadcrumb so a future 'user_stats add failed' after a go.mod bump is diagnosable in seconds.

Not a blocker for anything. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.
acceptance_criteria: If a modernc bump ever breaks repeated numbered-param binding, addAmount is updated (bind twice or use sql.Named) and services/userstats_sqlite_test.go confirms both llm_cost and revenue accumulate correctly.
